name: Claude Certified Architect Foundations - Udemy Practice Exams
description: Claude Certified Architect Foundations – Udemy Practice Exams

scenarios.text: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.

You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.

You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.

You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.

You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.

questions.question: This team keeps Terraform conventions that should load only while Claude edits files under terraform/, and it must guarantee that "terraform apply" never runs from a session. Which two steps achieve this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Save the conventions in ".claude/rules/terraform/" with no frontmatter, relying on the subdirectory to scope loading.
Add a "PreToolUse" hook in settings that blocks Bash commands containing "terraform apply".
Put the conventions and the apply ban in the root CLAUDE.md, marked IMPORTANT so they are reliably followed.
Create a ".claude/rules/" file with "paths: [\"terraform/**/*\"]" frontmatter containing the Terraform conventions.

questions.question: This team split its large CLAUDE.md into three files under ".claude/rules/" covering migrations, React components, and API handlers. Every session still loads all three at launch, even when only API code is being edited. What change makes each file load only when Claude works with matching files?

options.text: Run /compact at the start of each session with instructions to keep only the relevant rules.
Move each rule file into a subdirectory of ".claude/rules/" named for the code area it covers.
Reference each rule file from the root CLAUDE.md with "@" imports instead of keeping them in ".claude/rules/".
Add YAML frontmatter with a "paths" field of glob patterns to each rule file.

questions.question: A custom subagent runs the test suite during refactoring. When the suite times out partway, it reports only "tests could not be run", leaving the main session unable to decide what to do next. Which TWO reporting changes enable recovery? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the subagent name the failure type and the exact command it attempted.
Have the subagent map every error to a single "tests unavailable" status for simpler handling.
Have the subagent report a passing result on timeout so the main session continues uninterrupted.
Have the subagent include results from tests that finished plus a suggested narrower rerun.

questions.question: A developer is several hours into a database migration session that has been compacted repeatedly. Claude now quotes the wrong migration version, port number, and agreed timeout, and the compacted summaries describe these only as "connection settings were discussed." What change most reliably fixes this?

options.text: Keep the exact values in a structured facts file that Claude reads on every turn, outside the compacted history.
Run /compact less frequently so the session accumulates many more turns before any of the history is summarized.
Have Claude rate its confidence in each quoted value and ask you to confirm it whenever that confidence is low.
Give /compact a custom instruction to preserve every number and identifier verbatim in the summary it writes of older turns.

questions.question: A developer asks Claude Code to implement a date-normalization helper with several tricky edge cases. Each time the developer describes a new failing case in words, Claude's fix breaks a case that worked before. Which workflow change best stops this cycle?

options.text: Rewrite the request as a longer prose specification enumerating every edge case and expected result up front.
Switch to plan mode so Claude designs the helper's approach before it writes any code.
Run /compact after each round so earlier fixes stay in context and are not forgotten.
Have Claude write a test suite covering the edge cases first, then iterate on the failures until all pass.

questions.question: A developer is adding "context: fork" to the team's skills. One skill, /license-audit, crawls every dependency and prints a long findings transcript before a short verdict. Another, /api-style, only lists conventions to follow while editing the current file. How should "context: fork" be set?

options.text: Set "allowed-tools" on /license-audit to read-only tools so the audit produces a shorter transcript.
Set "context: fork" on /license-audit only and leave /api-style running inline in the main conversation.
Set "context: fork" on /api-style only, since its convention list is reference material rather than a task.
Set "context: fork" on both skills so that neither skill's content takes up space in the main conversation.

questions.question: A developer on this team wrapped the internal code search service as an MCP tool for Claude Code. When the backend times out, the tool returns the same plain "no results" message it returns for queries that really match nothing, and Claude then concludes a helper does not exist and writes a duplicate. What change to the tool fixes this?

options.text: Add a CLAUDE.md rule telling Claude to always re-run any search that comes back empty before it writes a new helper function.
Raise the tool's internal retry count on backend timeouts so that timeouts reach Claude less often.
Flag backend timeouts with "isError" true and a message saying the search timed out; return an empty list only for genuine no-match queries.
Attach a recent success-rate percentage for the search backend to every result so Claude can judge how trustworthy each empty answer is.

questions.question: This team's project CLAUDE.md states that Claude must never push directly to the main branch, yet in two sessions this month Claude pushed to main anyway. How should the team prevent this from recurring?

options.text: Add a PostToolUse hook on Bash that detects pushes to main and reports the violation to Claude.
Add a PreToolUse hook that matches Bash and denies any push targeting the main branch.
Move the rule to the top of CLAUDE.md and mark it IMPORTANT so it gets priority.
Move the rule into an Agent Skill that loads whenever Claude works with git commands.

questions.question: This team's monorepo has 14 service directories, each containing its own "migrations/" folder, and the same migration-authoring conventions should apply whenever Claude edits any migration file. Which configuration approach is most maintainable?

options.text: Add the conventions to the root CLAUDE.md so they are present in every session regardless of task.
Add one rule file under ".claude/rules/" with a "paths" glob that matches every migrations directory.
Copy a migrations-specific CLAUDE.md into each service's migrations directory so it loads there.
Package the conventions as a skill in ".claude/skills/" that developers invoke on demand before editing migrations.

questions.question: The team's /sprint-summary command combines benchmark numbers, the rationale for a database migration, and dependency audit findings. Its prompt formats everything as bulleted lists, and reviewers find the benchmarks and migration rationale hard to follow. What should the team change?

options.text: Specify per-section formats in the command prompt: a table for benchmarks, prose for the migration rationale, a list for audit findings.
Keep the single-list rule but mark it as IMPORTANT and add that every list must be easy to scan and complete.
Replace the list rule with an instruction to choose whichever layout reads best for each section, and leave the decision to Claude's judgment.
Split the command into three separate slash commands, one per content type, and have developers merge the outputs by hand.

questions.question: This team's monorepo keeps shared standards files in a top-level standards/ directory, and each package has its own CLAUDE.md owned by that package's maintainers, who know which standards apply to their code. How should each package's CLAUDE.md pick up only the standards that apply to it?

options.text: Move every standards file's content into the root CLAUDE.md so that all packages inherit the complete set at launch.
Have each maintainer copy the full text of the applicable standards files into their package's CLAUDE.md so it is self-contained.
Ask the developers working on each package to add the applicable standards to their own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md files.
Have each package's CLAUDE.md pull in only the applicable files with "@path" imports from the shared standards directory.

questions.question: The project CLAUDE.md for this team now contains a 70-line step-by-step dependency upgrade procedure that developers run only a few times a month, and Claude has started overlooking shorter coding rules placed below it. How should the team reorganize this content?

options.text: Keep the procedure in CLAUDE.md and prefix the coding rules with IMPORTANT so they are prioritized.
Move the upgrade procedure into a skill in .claude/skills/ and keep the coding rules in CLAUDE.md.
Move the procedure into each developer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so the project file stays shorter.
Keep the procedure in CLAUDE.md but split it into a separate file pulled in with an "@path" import.

questions.question: This team's documentation subagent in ".claude/agents/" has "tools: Write" only. It often stops to ask the main agent for function signatures. Once in a while, it also asks the main agent to run the test suite. Which TWO choices give the subagent the access it needs without giving it more than it needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep the rare test-suite runs with the main agent instead of adding Bash to the subagent.
Remove the "tools" field so the subagent inherits every tool the main agent has.
Add Read and Grep to the subagent's "tools" list so it can look up signatures itself.
Add Bash to the subagent's "tools" list so it can search code and run the test suite itself.

questions.question: In the extraction pipeline described above, a custom "lookup_vendor" tool returns an empty result both when the vendor database times out and when no vendor matches the extracted name. Records are being finalized with blank vendor fields in both cases. What change should the tool make?

options.text: Return a tool result with "is_error" set to true on timeout, and plain empty content when no vendor matches.
Have the model rate its confidence that the vendor exists and finalize the record only above a threshold.
Add a system prompt instruction telling Claude to ask a reviewer whenever the vendor field comes back empty.
Retry every empty lookup up to three times and treat the result as a genuine no-match only after that.

questions.question: This team has two extraction workloads: real-time intake, where operators wait for the results, and an overnight backlog of archived documents. The team wants to move work to the Message Batches API to cut cost. Which TWO actions are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Plan downstream deadlines around a window of up to 24 hours, because batch completion time is not guaranteed.
Move the overnight archive backlog to batch processing, since no one is waiting on those results.
Batch the real-time intake too, since most batches finish within an hour and the discount applies there as well.
Match each extraction result back to its source document by its position in the batch output file.

questions.question: The team defines an extraction tool whose "input_schema" matches the target record and leaves "tool_choice" at "auto". Their code parses the first content block as text with "JSON.parse", which fails intermittently. How should the code read the extraction instead?

options.text: Retry the request until the first content block parses as valid JSON, up to three attempts.
Select the content block whose "type" is "tool_use" and read its "input" object.
Instruct the model in the system prompt to emit no text before the JSON so the first block always parses.
Run a regex over the text block to isolate the JSON object before calling "JSON.parse".

questions.question: An engineer on this team has used one long Agent SDK session to catalog layout variations across 200 sample invoices. They now want to try two competing extraction schema designs, each starting from that analysis without influencing the other. Which approach fits?

options.text: Call "fork_session" on the baseline session and develop each schema design in its own fork.
Open two fresh sessions and paste a written summary of the layout catalog into each.
Resume the baseline session concurrently in two processes without forking and run one design in each.
Run both designs in sequence in the same session, telling the agent to disregard the first.

questions.question: In this system, the first-pass extraction stage sends each result to a reconciliation stage. Each result includes the full source passages and a long step-by-step reasoning narrative. The reconciliation stage has a tight context budget, and it now drops or misquotes fields. Which TWO changes address this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Remove the step-by-step reasoning field from the first-pass output and keep a per-field confidence score instead.
Move the reconciliation stage to a model with a larger context window and keep passing the full upstream output unchanged.
Define a JSON schema for the first-pass output containing extracted values, short evidence quotes, and page references.
Insert a prose summarization step that condenses each first-pass result before the reconciliation stage receives it.

questions.question: Reviewers for this system can manually check only one fifth of extracted documents. Today those documents are picked at random, so most field errors reach downstream systems unnoticed. How should the team decide which extractions get human review?

options.text: Add a per-field confidence value to the extraction schema and route low-confidence extractions to reviewers.
Instruct the model to omit any field it is not highly confident about so only certain values ship downstream.
Add a validation-retry loop that resends schema errors to the model until every extraction passes validation.
Route the longest documents to reviewers, since lengthy source material produces the most extraction errors.

questions.question: Claude reviews a 16-file pull request to the extraction pipeline in a single pass. Comments are thorough on the document parsers, shallow on the schema validators, and a null-handling pattern is flagged in one file but accepted unchanged in another. How should this team restructure the review?

options.text: Ask Claude to rate its confidence on each finding and discard those below a fixed threshold.
Run the single-pass review three times and keep only findings that appear in at least two runs.
Review each file separately for local issues, then run a distinct pass over cross-file data flows.
Move the review to a model with a larger context window so all 16 files fit comfortably.

questions.question: The extraction tool's schema declares "source" as a nullable string, and the instructions describe both citation styles. Some documents use a numbered bibliography instead of inline citations. For these documents, "source" always comes back null, even though the reference list contains it. What change most reliably fixes this?

options.text: Remove null from the allowed types of "source" so the schema forces a value for every document processed.
Return every null "source" result to Claude with a validation error so it retries the extraction attempt.
Add few-shot examples demonstrating "source" extraction from inline-citation and bibliography-style documents.
Add an emphatic instruction stating that "source" must always be taken from the document's reference list.

questions.question: Three extraction tools (one each for invoices, receipts, and purchase orders) are defined, and tool selection is left at its default. Assume the model and its settings support every "tool_choice" option. Documents arrive unlabeled, and about one in twenty responses is a short text description of the document instead of a tool call, which breaks the downstream parser. Which change ensures every document yields a structured extraction while Claude still picks the schema?

options.text: Keep the default "tool_choice" and resubmit any document whose response arrives as text rather than a tool call.
Force "tool_choice" to the invoice extraction tool because invoices are the most common document type in the stream.
Keep the default "tool_choice" and strengthen the system prompt to insist that a tool is called for every document.
Set "tool_choice" to the "any" type so a tool call is required while Claude still selects which extraction tool.

questions.question: This team runs two extraction workloads: an upload screen where a user waits on the page to confirm extracted fields, and a nightly backfill of 40,000 archived documents that feeds a dashboard refreshed each morning. To cut API cost, how should they apply the Message Batches API?

options.text: Submit both workloads as batches and poll for completion every few seconds so upload users receive results promptly.
Keep both workloads synchronous and reduce the number of extracted fields per document to lower token usage.
Submit both workloads as batches, falling back to a synchronous call whenever a batch has not finished within a minute.
Submit the nightly archive backfill as batches and keep the interactive upload screen on synchronous Messages API calls.

questions.question: The validation-retry loop resends each invoice with its specific validation error. Date-format failures clear after one retry, but "vendor_tax_id" failures persist through three retries because that ID exists only in a separate vendor registry that is never sent to Claude. What should the team do for these failures?

options.text: Add few-shot examples showing correctly extracted tax IDs from several differently structured invoices.
Stop retrying those invoices and include the matching vendor registry record in the extraction prompt.
Strengthen the retry instruction to state that the tax ID is mandatory and must never be left empty.
Raise the retry limit from three to six and include the prior incorrect extraction in each retry prompt.

questions.question: A coordinator hands each 50-document batch to an extraction subagent. When the document fetch tool times out on one file, the subagent drops its finished extractions and returns only "batch failed", so the coordinator re-runs the entire batch. What change best addresses this?

options.text: Have the subagent keep retrying the fetch until the document store responds so the coordinator never sees transient errors.
Have the subagent skip the unreachable file and report the batch as fully successful so that downstream processing is never interrupted by one document.
Have the subagent retry the timed-out fetch with backoff, then return finished extractions plus structured context for any file still failing.
Move all retry decisions to the coordinator by having the subagent return "batch failed" immediately on any tool error.

questions.question: The pipeline's review step reports that one handler function accepts an empty email string, and a failing unit test points to the exact line. A developer asks Claude Code to add the missing check. How should this change be carried out?

options.text: Enter plan mode first so Claude maps every caller of the handler before proposing the single check.
Delegate the work to an Explore subagent so the discovery output stays out of the main context.
Fork the session into two branches to compare alternative validation approaches before committing.
Run it as a direct execution request that names the file, the function, and the failing test.

questions.question: A developer on this team must restructure how review findings move from the JSON output into inline PR comments. The work spans dozens of files, several designs are viable, and the developer is unfamiliar with that part of the code. How should the developer proceed?

options.text: Enter plan mode so Claude explores the code and proposes a plan to approve before editing.
Use direct execution with detailed instructions given in advance that spell out the intended file structure.
Run the restructuring unattended with "claude -p" so the pipeline applies it without review.
Run direct execution incrementally and switch to plan mode if complexity appears.

questions.question: This team's review service calls the Messages API with a "fetch_file" tool so Claude can request imports and tests mid-review. After the service retrieves a requested file, how must it deliver the contents so Claude can continue the analysis?

options.text: Embed the fetched file contents in the "fetch_file" tool's description so Claude reads it on its next evaluation pass.
Append a user message containing a "tool_result" block whose "tool_use_id" matches the request, then resend the full history.
Send the fetched file contents as a plain user text message in a new request, since the API keeps earlier turns server-side.
Add a message with a dedicated "tool" role carrying the file contents so the API routes it to the pending request.

questions.question: This team's review prompt spells out the required finding format in detail, yet findings still alternate between concrete fixes and vague notes. Which TWO changes best restore consistent, actionable output? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the model attach a self-rated confidence score to each finding and discard anything below a fixed threshold.
Add two to four examples that show the exact finding layout: file location, issue, severity, and a concrete fix.
Rewrite the format instructions in capital letters with phrases like ALWAYS and NEVER to raise their priority over other guidance.
Use real cases from the codebase as examples, including ambiguous ones, and show the reasoning behind each verdict.

questions.question: The structured review findings this team emits use a "category" enum limited to "bug", "security", "performance", and "style". Licensing and accessibility findings are being squeezed into "style" and routed to the wrong reviewers. Which schema change best handles findings outside the listed categories?

options.text: Make the category field optional so the model can leave it empty whenever no listed value fits a finding.
Replace the enum with an unconstrained string so the model can label each finding with whatever category it sees fit.
Add an "other" value to the category enum together with a free-text field that describes the uncategorized finding.
Add a prompt instruction telling the model to choose the closest existing category whenever a finding does not fit clearly.

questions.question: A developer on this team wants to experiment with a stricter version of the shared /pr-review skill in local sessions, running it side by side with the team's version for comparison, without changing what teammates or the pipeline see. How should the variant be set up?

options.text: Commit the stricter variant as "pr-review-strict" in the repository's .claude/skills/ directory.
Add the stricter review rules to the developer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so they apply in every local session.
Create the stricter variant in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name such as "pr-review-strict".
Create the stricter variant in ~/.claude/skills/pr-review/ so it loads only in the developer's own sessions.

questions.question: A developer reports that this team's review prompt produces far fewer style findings in their local Claude Code session than when the CI job runs the identical prompt against the same repository checkout. What is the best first diagnostic step?

options.text: Run /context in the developer's local session and check the Memory files list against what CI loads.
Re-run the CI job several times and keep the run whose findings match the developer's local results.
Run "claude doctor" on the CI runner to list any settings entries that were rejected when the job started.
Add stronger wording to the project CLAUDE.md instructing Claude to ignore style issues during review.

questions.question: This team's pipeline step launches the "claude" command with the review prompt as an argument, but every job waits with no activity until the runner's timeout kills it and no review is ever produced. What change fixes the step?

options.text: Set "--permission-mode acceptEdits" so the run never pauses waiting for approval of file edits.
Run the command with the "-p" flag so it processes the prompt, prints the result, and exits.
Add "--output-format json" so the result is emitted as machine-readable output the pipeline can parse.
Raise the pipeline step's timeout so the review has enough time to finish before the runner kills it.

questions.question: The review agent in this pipeline reads CI results from three MCP servers, two of them third-party, that return mixed formats: Unix timestamps, ISO 8601 dates, and numeric build states. It sometimes misreports a failed build as passing in PR comments. What is the most maintainable fix?

options.text: Expose a custom "normalize_result" MCP tool and instruct the agent to call it after every CI data fetch.
Document each server's timestamp and build state conventions in the project CLAUDE.md so the agent interprets them.
Register a "PostToolUse" hook matched to those tools that rewrites each result into one consistent format.
Build proxy MCP servers around the third-party ones that reformat their responses before returning them.

questions.question: The review step in this pipeline emits findings as JSON, and a validator rejects roughly one run in ten because a finding's "line" value falls outside the pull request diff. The team wants the step to recover automatically on the next attempt. What should the retry request contain?

options.text: Include the original diff plus a general note that the previous attempt was invalid and must be regenerated.
Resubmit the same prompt unchanged, relying on a fresh sample to land every line inside the diff.
Include the original diff, the rejected output, and the exact validation error identifying the out-of-range finding.
Resend the original prompt with stronger wording insisting that every cited line number must fall inside the diff.

questions.question: The pipeline's test generator receives the existing tests for each changed file. When those tests cover only one branch of a conditional, the generator is inconsistent: sometimes it proposes a test for the other branch, and sometimes it says the function is already covered. Detailed coverage instructions have not helped. What addition most reliably fixes this inconsistency?

options.text: Include the project's entire test suite in the prompt so the model has complete coverage context.
Run the generator three times per changed file and keep only tests proposed in at least two runs.
Add two or three examples of partly tested functions that show whether to test the other branch and why.
Add an explicit rule stating that every untested conditional branch must always receive a new test.

questions.question: When a changed function depends on a helper defined in another file, the automated reviewer behaves inconsistently: it flags a bug without reading the helper, reads the helper and still flags correct code, or skips the case entirely. Prose rules describing when to read, flag, or skip have not fixed this. What addition is most effective?

options.text: Add an emphatic rule that the reviewer must read every imported file before reporting any finding on a pull request.
Ask the reviewer to rate its confidence on each cross-file finding and drop any finding below a fixed threshold.
Add two to four examples of ambiguous cross-file cases, each showing the action taken and why it beat the alternatives.
Add twenty or more examples covering every import pattern in the codebase so no cross-file case is left unaddressed.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent keeps running built-in Grep over downloaded files instead of calling its MCP tool "search_corpus". That tool returns ranked passages with source citations and page numbers, but its description says only "Searches research documents." Which TWO changes most directly fix this preference? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a rule to the subagent's system prompt stating it must always call search_corpus instead of Grep for every lookup.
Add text to the tool's description saying when to use it instead of plain text search over the files.
Rename the tool to grep_corpus so the agent associates it with the built-in search tool it already favors.
Expand the description to list the ranked passages, source citations, and page numbers it returns that Grep cannot.

questions.question: The team's shared MCP configuration must supply the search API key and the hosted document service's bearer token to every teammate, without committing either secret to the repository. Which TWO practices achieve this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set the document service entry's "headers" field to "Authorization: Bearer ${DOCS_API_TOKEN}" so the token expands at runtime.
Reference the search key as "${SEARCH_API_KEY}" in the stdio server's "env" field so it expands from each developer's shell.
Write the literal secrets into ".mcp.json" at the project root and add that file to ".gitignore" so the keys never reach the remote.
Put the real key as the fallback in "${SEARCH_API_KEY:-sk-live-9f3a}" so the configuration works before anyone sets a shell variable.

questions.question: The web search subagent's MCP search tool sets "isError" to true whenever its result list is empty, so the coordinator retries zero-match queries as if the search service were down. How should the tool report a query that legitimately matches no sources?

options.text: Silently retry the search with broader terms until at least one source can be returned.
Return a JSON-RPC protocol error so the MCP host handles the condition instead of the model.
Return a normal result with "isError" false and content stating that no sources matched the query.
Return "isError" true with an "errorCategory" of transient so the coordinator knows to retry later.

questions.question: Reports often have thin sections even though the first breakdown of the topic was correct: a grid-storage report covered batteries in depth but gave hydrogen only two sentences. The team wants such gaps closed automatically before report generation. Which design accomplishes this?

options.text: Have the coordinator evaluate the synthesis for gaps, re-delegate targeted searches, and re-run synthesis.
Let the synthesis subagent spawn its own search subagent directly whenever it finds a thin section.
Have the report generation subagent annotate thin sections as known coverage limitations in the report.
Strengthen the synthesis subagent's prompt to demand thorough, balanced treatment of every subtopic.

questions.question: Yesterday a document analysis session named "corpus-review" analyzed 40 source PDFs for an upcoming report. Overnight, a teammate replaced three of those PDFs with corrected versions. How should the team continue the analysis today?

options.text: Start a fresh session with no prior context and have the agent re-read all 40 PDFs from scratch.
Resume "corpus-review" and run /compact first so the summary replaces any stale tool results before continuing.
Resume "corpus-review" and open by naming the three replaced PDFs, asking for re-analysis limited to those files.
Resume "corpus-review" and continue synthesis directly, since the restored transcript already holds the analysis of all 40 PDFs.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent exposes three tools: extract_metadata, enrich_citations, and summarize_section. In some runs it calls enrich_citations first, producing citations with missing dates. The team needs extract_metadata guaranteed as the first call on every document. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Set "tool_choice" to the "any" type so the subagent must begin with a tool call rather than text.
Set "strict" to true on the extract_metadata definition so its schema is enforced before other tools run.
Add a system prompt rule stating that metadata extraction must always precede citation enrichment.
Set "tool_choice" to the "tool" type naming extract_metadata on the first request for each document.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent outputs structured records with claim, quote, source, and publication date fields, and a human currently reviews every record. Overall accuracy measures 97%. What should the team do before removing human review from high-confidence records?

options.text: Have the synthesis subagent flag records whose figures look unusual compared to other sources.
Remove review from every record the model rates high-confidence, since 97% already exceeds the target.
Measure accuracy separately by document type and by extracted field before trusting the overall figure.
Add a validation-retry loop so schema violations are corrected before records reach reviewers.

questions.question: A team is designing the coordinator's control flow. Research requests vary widely: some need only web search, while others require document analysis that then reveals gaps calling for a second search round. How should the coordinator decide which subagent to invoke next?

options.text: Add a keyword classifier that maps each request to a predetermined subagent sequence before the run starts.
Prompt the coordinator with the research goal and let it choose each subagent from intermediate results.
Add a PreToolUse hook that rewrites each delegation to the next subagent in a predetermined order.
Hard-code the search, analysis, synthesis, and report subagent calls as a fixed sequence in application code.

questions.question: Asked to trace how citations flow from the search subagent to the report generator in this system's codebase, an agent with Read, Grep, and Glob reads every file under "src/" and exhausts its context. Which TWO instructions correct its exploration strategy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Read every file under the source directory first so nothing is missed before reasoning.
Grep for citation-related identifiers to find likely entry points and call sites.
Read the files Grep returned, then follow their imports to the next files to trace.
Spawn one subagent per source file so each file is read in its own isolated context.

questions.question: While developing this system in Claude Code, a developer wants to try an MCP server that searches academic papers with the web search subagent before suggesting it to the team, and teammates should not see it yet. Where should the server be configured?

options.text: Add the server under user scope in the developer's own "~/.claude.json" file.
Document the server's launch command in the project's CLAUDE.md so Claude starts it on demand.
Add the server to the project's ".mcp.json" and tell teammates to ignore its tools for now.
Register the server in ".claude/settings.local.json" since that file stays out of version control.

questions.question: A teammate suggests letting the document analysis subagent hand its findings straight to the synthesis subagent. Which two design choices keep the system consistent with the hub-and-spoke pattern? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Rely on the synthesis subagent inheriting the coordinator's conversation history instead of passing findings explicitly.
Keep error handling in the coordinator so it sees every subagent failure and decides recovery in one place.
Return the analysis results to the coordinator, which includes them explicitly in the synthesis subagent's prompt.
Let the analysis subagent send its findings directly to the synthesis subagent to remove a coordinator hop.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent has the built-in Read tool and an MCP tool "fetch_source_document", described only as "Retrieves a document", that returns text with its source URL and page anchors. The subagent keeps using Read on local copies of the files instead, so findings reach synthesis without citation metadata. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Expand the MCP tool's description to highlight the source URL and page anchors that Read cannot provide.
Add a system prompt rule telling the subagent to always prefer MCP tools over built-in ones.
Have the synthesis subagent re-fetch every document after analysis to reconstruct the missing citations.
Add few-shot examples to the subagent prompt showing it calling "fetch_source_document" first.

questions.question: The report-generation subagent needs to replace one of nine identical "Source: pending" markers in a drafted Markdown report, and its Edit call fails because the target text is not unique. Which TWO approaches reliably complete the change? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Write just the corrected section and rely on Write to merge it into the existing report.
Retry Edit with an "old_string" that includes enough surrounding lines to match the intended marker only.
Read the full report, then Write the complete contents with only the intended marker changed.
Retry Edit with "replace_all" set to true so the uniqueness requirement no longer blocks the call.

questions.question: The coordinator receives an open-ended research topic whose relevant subtopics cannot be known in advance. Which two practices should the coordinator apply when decomposing the work? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Generate follow-up subtasks from what earlier subagents discover rather than fixing the full task list at the start.
Run an initial broad scoping pass to map the topic's main areas before assigning detailed subagent tasks.
Define the complete list of subagent assignments up front so every run follows the same fixed, reproducible pipeline.
Have each subagent rate its own confidence that its area is covered and re-run only the low scorers.

questions.question: Logs show the web search and document analysis subagents repeatedly investigate the same subtopics, nearly doubling token usage without broadening the research. Which two changes most effectively reduce this duplication? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the coordinator state in each delegation prompt which subtopics that subagent must not cover.
Have the coordinator split the topic into distinct subtopics and assign each subagent its own set.
Add a shared log where each subagent records its current focus so the other can avoid it.
Let both subagents cover the full topic, then have the coordinator deduplicate the overlapping findings.

questions.question: The coordinator session has finished gathering and aggregating findings on a topic, an expensive phase the team does not want to repeat. They now want to try two different report structures from that same aggregated baseline, with neither attempt seeing the other's output. How should they proceed?

options.text: Start two fresh sessions and seed each with a hand-written summary of the aggregated findings as the first message.
Resume the coordinator session with "fork_session" enabled twice, giving each report structure its own branch from the baseline.
Resume the session once and ask the coordinator to draft both report structures within the same turn for comparison.
Resume the same session ID twice in sequence, instructing the second run to disregard the first report structure it produced.

questions.question: The coordinator's system prompt defines the required citation format, yet the document analysis subagent returns uncited findings and sometimes asks which document it should analyze. Which two changes correct this behavior? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add the citation format rules to the document analysis subagent's own system prompt in its "AgentDefinition".
Strengthen the coordinator's system prompt to state that every subagent must apply the citation format.
Start the subagent after the coordinator has discussed the document, so the discussion is already in its history.
Include the full document text and the research question directly in each delegation prompt.

questions.question: The coordinator escalates to a human editor mid-research when two credible sources materially conflict on a key statistic. The editor cannot see the agent transcript. Which two elements should the handoff include? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Include the coordinator's recommended resolution and its reasoning, so the editor can approve or override it.
Include a self-rated confidence score for the entire draft report so the editor can quickly judge whether to intervene.
Include the request identifier, the conflicting values with their sources and dates, and what remains unresearched.
Include every raw search result and document excerpt the subagents gathered, so the editor can rebuild the analysis.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent receives all twelve source documents in one prompt and analyzes some documents in depth and others only briefly, and it judges similar claims in contradictory ways. Which two changes to its pipeline most directly address this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Move the subagent to a model with a larger context window so that all twelve documents fit comfortably in one pass.
Run a separate analysis pass for each document that outputs structured per-document findings.
Run the full twelve-document analysis three times and keep only findings that appear in at least two runs.
Add a second integration pass that reconciles per-document findings and flags cross-document contradictions.

questions.question: The coordinator runs multi-hour research tasks that trigger several context compactions. After each compaction it re-dispatches subtopics that subagents already completed and misquotes figures they returned earlier. What change best preserves this information across compactions?

options.text: Have the coordinator append each subagent's findings and task status to a scratchpad file that it re-reads after compaction.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the coordinator to retain all completed subtopics and returned figures across compactions.
Include the coordinator's full conversation history in every subagent prompt so completed findings are retained in subagent context.
Raise the compaction threshold so the coordinator's conversation is summarized less often during long research runs.

questions.question: After the coordinator completes a costly analysis of a large document corpus in one session, the team wants to compare a chronological synthesis and a thematic synthesis, each starting from that analysis without influencing the other. What should they do?

options.text: Start two new sessions and paste a written summary of the completed analysis into each as the opening prompt.
Run the first strategy in the original session, then instruct the agent to discard it before running the second.
Resume the same analysis session ID in two concurrent runs, giving each run a different synthesis instruction.
Resume the analysis session twice with "fork_session" enabled, running each synthesis strategy in its own fork.

questions.question: The "load_document" tool used by the document analysis subagent returns "Document could not be loaded" on every failure. Logs show the subagent retrying paywalled documents repeatedly yet abandoning those that hit a single timeout. Which change to the tool's response best corrects this?

options.text: Raise the subagent's maximum turn budget so repeated load attempts can finish before it gives up.
Add a system prompt rule telling the subagent to retry every failed load exactly once before moving on.
Have the coordinator intercept load failures and retry them centrally before the subagent sees any result.
Return "isError" true with an error category, a retryable flag, and a readable message.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent's "load_document" tool fails when a requested file is in a repository its service account cannot read. The tool currently labels this a transient error, so the subagent retries repeatedly before giving up. How should the tool report this failure instead?

options.text: Keep the "errorCategory" as transient but raise the retry limit and add exponential backoff between successive attempts.
Return an "isError" true result with metadata marking a non-retryable permission failure for the subagent to escalate.
Return an "isError" true result whose metadata labels it a validation failure with a hint to fix the identifier.
Return a successful result with empty content so the subagent proceeds without the document.

questions.question: The team's /pr-summary command instructs Claude to render benchmark numbers as a table, the design rationale as prose, and follow-up tasks as a checklist. Across runs, Claude still often turns the table into bullets and the rationale into a list. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Mark the formatting instructions as "IMPORTANT" and restate them at the end of the command prompt.
Add an example summary to the command file that shows each section rendered in its intended format.
Run the command through "claude -p" with "--json-schema" so every summary is validated against one structure.
Render all three sections as markdown tables so the output format no longer varies between runs.

questions.question: This team ran Claude Code across 900 legacy modules to extract each module's owner, SLA tier, and data classification from inconsistent header comments into a structured service catalog. Reviewers can manually check only about 150 entries. How should the team decide which entries receive human review?

options.text: Measure aggregate accuracy on a pilot of 100 modules and auto-accept all entries if the pilot exceeds 97 percent.
Review a uniformly random sample of 150 entries and auto-accept all remaining entries, since random sampling represents the whole catalog fairly.
Strengthen the extraction prompt so Claude resolves contradictory headers itself, then auto-accept every entry the run produces.
Score confidence per extracted field, calibrate thresholds on a labeled sample, and route low-confidence or contradictory entries to reviewers.

questions.question: A developer on this team wrote the shared API conventions into "CLAUDE.local.md" at the repository root. Their own sessions follow the conventions, but teammates who pull the repository report that Claude ignores them. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Add the conventions to ".claude/settings.json" as a committed project setting applied to every teammate.
Have each teammate paste the conventions into their own user-level "~/.claude/CLAUDE.md" file.
Move the conventions into the committed root CLAUDE.md so every teammate who pulls receives them.
Import "CLAUDE.local.md" from the root CLAUDE.md with an "@" path so the committed file pulls it in.

questions.question: Test files sit beside the code they test across many subdirectories, and the team wants testing conventions loaded only when a test file is touched. The rule in ".claude/rules/testing.md" sets its "paths" field to "*.test.tsx", but nothing loads when Claude edits "src/components/Button.test.tsx". What should change?

options.text: Remove the "paths" frontmatter entirely so the testing conventions load unconditionally in every session.
Add a directory-level CLAUDE.md containing the testing conventions inside each folder that holds tests.
Convert the testing conventions into a skill in ".claude/skills/" that developers invoke before editing tests.
Change the pattern to "**/*.test.tsx" so the rule matches test files in any directory.

questions.question: A developer used Claude Code to generate a database migration script. It handles typical rows but keeps failing on null values. The developer has described the problem in words twice, and the script still fails. What should the developer provide next?

options.text: Restate the null-handling requirement in the prompt with stronger emphasis markers so Claude treats it as the highest priority.
Switch to plan mode so Claude re-reads the entire migration script and proposes an approach before editing it again.
Paste the full production data export into the conversation so Claude can discover every null variant on its own.
Give Claude a few sample rows containing null, empty, and missing values, each paired with the exact migrated output expected.

questions.question: A custom discovery subagent finds every call site of a deprecated helper before the main session deletes it. When its search errors out partway through the repository, the subagent reports zero call sites and the deletion proceeds. Which reporting change prevents this?

options.text: Have the subagent keep retrying the failed search until it succeeds before returning anything to the main session.
Have the subagent attach a self-rated confidence score describing how complete its empty result is.
Have the main session repeat the full discovery itself whenever the subagent reports zero call sites.
Have the subagent return a distinct error carrying the underlying failure message instead of a zero-match result.

questions.question: A developer asks Claude Code to generate unit tests for a payment module, and several of the new cases repeat scenarios already covered in the module's existing spec file. What should the developer change in the next request?

options.text: Generate the tests, then send a second prompt asking Claude to compare them with the suite and remove overlaps.
Add a line to the project CLAUDE.md stating that generated tests must never repeat scenarios already in the suite.
Reference the tests directory with "@" so that every existing test file is loaded before generation starts.
Reference the module's existing spec file with "@" and ask Claude to add only scenarios it does not already cover.

questions.question: This team runs a Claude Code coordinator with several subagents to migrate 60 modules to a new logging library. When the process crashes partway through, the restarted coordinator starts over and re-migrates every module. Which design lets the restarted run resume from where the previous one stopped?

options.text: Run /compact before each migration phase so the coordinator's context stays small enough to survive a restart.
Add automatic retries so the coordinator re-spawns every subagent after a crash until all modules finish.
Instruct the coordinator to keep a running list of completed modules inside its own conversation context.
Have each subagent record its finished modules in a shared manifest file that the coordinator reads on restart.

questions.question: This team's /audit command concatenates four subagents' raw scan output into one long prompt that produces a consolidated report. The report reliably covers the first and last subagents' findings but misses critical issues from the middle two. How should the aggregated input be restructured?

options.text: Open the input with a key-findings summary and separate each subagent's detailed results under explicit section headings.
Add a system prompt instruction stating that every section of the input must be weighted equally.
Rotate which subagent's output appears first on each run so that every scanner receives the top position over time.
Run the consolidation prompt a second time and merge both resulting reports to recover any findings that were dropped.

questions.question: A developer wants a personal, modified version of the team's shared /gen-tests skill for their own sessions. Teammates must not be affected, and the developer still needs to be able to run the team's original /gen-tests on their machine. How should the variant be set up?

options.text: Set "skillOverrides" in personal settings so /gen-tests resolves to the modified instructions.
Create the variant under ~/.claude/skills/ using a distinct skill name such as gen-tests-local.
Place the variant at ~/.claude/skills/gen-tests/SKILL.md so it never enters the repository.
Commit the variant to the repository's .claude/skills/ under a separate name so it stays versioned.

questions.question: The team's /triage command, run with "claude -p" on new bug reports, hands a bug to an engineer when Claude rates its confidence below 6 or the report sounds frustrated. As a result, easy reports written angrily go to an engineer, while hard reports written calmly are left for Claude to fix. Which TWO changes make the hand-off decision reliable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Hand off whenever the fix would require a decision that the repository's conventions do not cover.
Enable extended thinking for the triage step so the self-rated confidence score becomes better calibrated.
Raise the confidence threshold from 6 to 8 so more borderline reports are routed to an engineer.
Replace both signals with explicit hand-off criteria and few-shot examples of fix versus hand-off cases.

questions.question: A developer is replacing ad hoc print statements with structured logging across a large service. Listing every call site would fill the main conversation before design starts. The design and the implementation also need to stay consistent with each other. How should the work be organized?

options.text: Instruct Claude in the prompt to report only the relevant call sites and keep every search result brief.
Start a fresh session per phase, recording the discovered call sites in CLAUDE.md for the next session to load.
Delegate the call-site discovery to the Explore subagent, then design and implement in the main conversation.
Keep discovery in the main conversation and run /compact after each batch of search results to reclaim space.

questions.question: This team wrote a skill in .claude/skills/ that holds the rule "use named exports, never default exports". Claude follows the rule in some sessions and ignores it in others, depending on whether the skill happened to be loaded. What should the team change?

options.text: Move the export rule into the project-level CLAUDE.md so it loads in every session.
Ask every developer to invoke the skill manually at the start of each session.
Add "context: fork" to the skill's frontmatter so the rule survives context compaction.
Rewrite the skill's "description" with more trigger keywords so Claude loads it more often.

questions.question: A developer is debugging a legacy billing module across several daily Claude Code sessions while teammates keep committing changes to it. Each new session, Claude repeats earlier discovery work and no longer knows the conclusions reached the day before. Which TWO practices address this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Append each session's findings to the project CLAUDE.md so they load automatically for every developer in every session.
Resume the prior day's session with "--resume" so its accumulated tool results stay available for the next round of debugging.
Begin each new session by directing Claude to read the scratchpad file and recent git history before any further exploration.
Have Claude record confirmed findings in a scratchpad file in the repository as it works, rather than only in the conversation.

questions.question: The automated reviewer judges catch-all exception handlers inconsistently. This team added four examples, each a code snippet labeled only "report" or "skip". Handlers that closely match an example are judged correctly, but new variants still receive inconsistent verdicts. What change most effectively improves generalization?

options.text: Have the reviewer assign a confidence score to each handler finding and drop those below a threshold.
Add an instruction telling the reviewer to use its best judgment on handlers that do not match an example.
Expand the example set to twenty or more snippets so more catch-all variants are covered directly.
Add a short rationale to each example explaining why reporting or skipping beat the alternative.

questions.question: A pull request review from the pipeline returns six findings: three interacting issues inside a shared retry helper and three unrelated single-line fixes elsewhere. How should the developer give these findings to Claude Code? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Delegate each of the six findings to its own isolated subagent so the fixes proceed in parallel.
Batch all six findings into one message so Claude resolves the entire review in a single pass.
Address the three unrelated single-line fixes one at a time, verifying each before moving on.
Send the three interacting retry-helper findings together in one message so Claude fixes them jointly.

questions.question: After Claude Code generates a fix in the pipeline, the team wants a second instance to review that fix with no access to the generator's reasoning. Which TWO practices correctly set up this independent review? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Pass the changed file paths and diff explicitly to the reviewer, since it cannot see the generator's prior tool results.
Launch the review as a separate Claude Code run that is given only the diff and the review criteria.
Resume the generation session with a review prompt so the reviewer retains everything the generator already discovered.
Enable extended thinking during generation so Claude deliberates more carefully before finalizing the fix.

questions.question: The pipeline's review findings are emitted through a tool whose "category" field is an enum of "security", "correctness", "performance", and "style". Logs show licensing and accessibility issues being forced into "style", where developers routinely dismiss them. Which schema change best preserves these findings?

options.text: Add a self-rated confidence score to each finding so weakly categorized ones can be filtered out.
Add a prompt instruction to report only findings that clearly belong to one of the four categories.
Add an "other" value to the enum alongside a free-text field describing the issue type.
Make the category field nullable so Claude can leave it empty when no listed category fits.

questions.question: Metrics for the automated review show that documentation and naming findings are wrong roughly half the time, while correctness and security findings are rarely wrong. Developers now merge without reading any findings. What should the team do first?

options.text: Tighten reporting thresholds across all categories equally so the blended false-positive rate falls to an acceptable level.
Keep every category active but attach the model's self-rated confidence to each finding so developers can triage faster.
Add an instruction telling the model to apply much stricter judgment to documentation and naming findings before reporting them.
Remove the documentation and naming categories from the review prompt for now, and reinstate them once their criteria are reworked.

questions.question: The test-generation step in this pipeline emits each suggested test through a tool whose schema marks "existing_test_file" as required. For modules that have no tests yet, Claude fills the field with plausible-looking paths that do not exist, and the pipeline fails when it opens them. What change most directly addresses this?

options.text: Add a validation-retry loop that returns the missing-path error so Claude can correct the value.
Make "existing_test_file" optional and nullable so Claude can return null when no test file exists.
Add an instruction to the prompt stating that file paths must never be invented under any circumstances.
Add few-shot examples showing correctly populated paths for modules that already have test files.

questions.question: This team's review prompt tells Claude to report only findings it is at least 90% sure about, yet developers still receive comments on naming, import order, and local helper patterns the team accepts. What prompt change best removes this noise?

options.text: Have Claude attach a self-rated confidence score to each finding and drop low scores during post-processing.
Replace the threshold with explicit lists of what to report, such as logic and security bugs, and what to skip.
Run the review three times on each pull request and keep only findings that appear in every run.
Raise the stated threshold to 99% and add that only findings certain to be real defects should appear.

questions.question: The review job runs with "--output-format json" and "--json-schema", and every finding parses without errors. However, "ticket_id" arrives as "PROJ-482", "proj 482", or "#482", depending on how the PR description wrote it. The step that builds the issue tracker link then fails. What change best fixes this?

options.text: Instruct Claude to copy the ticket reference exactly as it appears in the PR description or commit message.
Add a post-processing step that strips every non-digit character from the ticket string before building the link.
State a standard ticket format in the prompt with rules for converting each variant found in PR text.
Enable strict schema enforcement so the API rejects any ticket value that is not in the standard form.

questions.question: This team's pipeline writes a test suite before implementation and asks Claude to make it pass. When tests fail, the pipeline re-prompts with "Some tests failed, try again," and runs rarely converge. What change would most improve the loop?

options.text: Include the failing test names and assertion output in each retry prompt so Claude can target the actual failures.
Raise the maximum number of retry attempts per run so Claude has more chances to converge on a passing implementation.
Ask Claude to rate its confidence that the implementation is correct before each resubmission and retry only when it is low.
Rewrite each retry prompt with a more detailed prose description of the behavior the tests already expect.

questions.question: The pipeline defines three extraction tools (one each for code diffs, CI failure logs, and dependency manifest changes) and sets "tool_choice" to the "any" type because artifacts arrive unlabeled. Every artifact now returns a tool call, but roughly one in five failure logs is routed to the diff tool. What change best fixes the misrouting?

options.text: Rewrite each tool description to spell out what its artifact type looks like and when to prefer it over the other two.
Add a retry step that resubmits any artifact whose extracted output fails validation against the chosen tool's schema.
Change tool selection to force the diff-extraction tool so every artifact is processed with a single consistent schema.
Return tool selection to its default so Claude can answer in text when it is unsure which extraction tool applies.

questions.question: This team wants every automated review finding to carry a confidence value so a separate verification stage can route findings for a second look. Which TWO practices make that confidence useful for routing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Check the reported confidence against a labeled set of findings before using it to set routing thresholds.
Instruct the review prompt to withhold any finding whose confidence falls below a fixed threshold before output.
Run the review three times and average each finding's confidence so routing uses a smoother signal.
Ask the review to report every finding, including uncertain ones, and filter by confidence in a later pass.

questions.question: A trial ran the nightly test-generation job through the Message Batches API, and every batch finished in well under an hour. A developer now proposes routing the pre-merge review check, which must finish before a pull request can merge, through batches as well to save cost. How should the team respond?

options.text: Move the pre-merge check to batches but poll the batch status and fall back to a synchronous call after one hour.
Keep the pre-merge check on the synchronous Messages API and leave only the nightly job on batches.
Move the pre-merge check to batches with "stream" set to true so results are delivered as soon as each request completes.
Move the pre-merge check to batches and submit each pull request as its own single-request batch so it is processed faster.

questions.question: The reviewer kept flagging intentionally empty catch blocks that carry a best-effort cleanup comment. The team added few-shot examples marking that idiom acceptable, and now the reviewer also ignores catch blocks that silently swallow real errors. How should the examples be revised?

options.text: Keep the examples and ask the reviewer to attach a self-rated confidence score to each finding.
Remove the examples and instruct the reviewer to flag every empty catch block as a bug.
Add more examples of the accepted idiom so the pattern is learned more firmly.
Pair each acceptable idiom with a similar-looking genuine defect, stating why only one is reportable.

questions.question: A developer on this team used plan mode to address a CI finding that test fixtures are duplicated across 40 modules; Claude proposed a shared fixture design the developer agrees with. What should happen next?

options.text: Copy the fixture design into the project CLAUDE.md so future sessions apply it automatically.
Stay in plan mode and instruct Claude to begin editing each module listed in the plan.
Approve the plan so the session leaves plan mode and Claude implements the agreed design.
Open a fresh session and paste the plan text as the opening implementation prompt.

questions.question: A CI job asks Claude to return test-case suggestions for each pull request as JSON in the response text. The pipeline step that posts the PR comment sometimes rejects the output as malformed or missing a required field. Which change most reliably eliminates these rejections?

options.text: Rewrite the instruction to demand complete, valid JSON only, listing every required field and forbidding any commentary.
Wrap the comment-posting step in a retry loop that re-sends the diff whenever it rejects the payload as malformed or incomplete.
Define a test-suggestion tool with "strict" set to true whose input schema is the payload structure, and read the "tool_use" input.
Add a post-processing stage that repairs malformed JSON with a lenient parser and fills missing fields with default values.

questions.question: The team's system prompt tells the agent to "search for relevant context before answering." A connected MCP server exposes a "search_tickets" tool, and logs show the agent calling it for code questions instead of Grep. Which TWO changes most directly fix this misrouting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reword the instruction to name the intended behavior, such as using Grep to find code, instead of a generic "search" directive.
Add boundary language to the "search_tickets" description stating that it covers issue tracker tickets only, not source code.
Set "tool_choice" to "any" so the agent is guaranteed to invoke some tool before answering any code question.
Add a capitalized rule stating the agent MUST NEVER call "search_tickets" unless the user explicitly references a ticket number.

questions.question: The team's /scaffold-module skill creates several boilerplate files on each invocation. Developers are interrupted by a permission prompt for every file write. They want file writes approved without a prompt, but only while this skill runs. What should the team change?

options.text: Add an "allowed-tools" entry listing Write to the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter.
Invoke the skill in plan mode so the file writes proceed without prompts.
State in the skill's instructions that file writes are pre-approved and need no confirmation.
Add Write to "permissions.allow" in the project's .claude/settings.json file.

questions.question: A team wants the agent to read GitHub issues and pull requests, and also to query an internal on-call catalog, a service with a proprietary HTTP API that lists the on-call owner of each microservice. A developer proposes writing custom MCP servers for both. What should the team do instead?

options.text: Use an existing GitHub MCP server and build a custom MCP server only for the internal on-call catalog.
Postpone both integrations until the Anthropic Directory lists a reviewed connector for each system.
Have the agent call the GitHub REST API through Bash with curl instead of connecting any MCP server.
Build custom MCP servers for both systems so the team fully controls tool names and descriptions.

questions.question: An engineer wants this agent to add caching to a poorly understood legacy service. The agent's tools list contains only "Read", "Grep", "Glob", and "Write". Which TWO steps let the agent use the interview pattern before implementation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Delegate the questioning to a subagent spawned through the Agent tool so the main context stays uncluttered.
Prompt the agent to question the engineer about invalidation rules, failure modes, and tradeoffs before it writes code.
Add "AskUserQuestion" to the agent's tools list so its clarifying questions can actually reach the engineer.
Have the agent rate its own confidence in a design and ask questions only when that score falls below a threshold.

questions.question: The team connects an MCP server whose "search_symbols" tool searches a prebuilt index of dozens of repositories, but the tool's description says only "Searches code." The agent nearly always uses Grep instead, missing matches outside the current checkout. What should the team change first?

options.text: Add a system prompt rule instructing the agent to always call "search_symbols" before falling back to Grep for any code search task.
Remove Grep from the agent's allowed tools so that "search_symbols" becomes the only available way to search code across the repositories.
Rewrite the "search_symbols" description to state what it returns, when to use it instead of Grep, and its cross-repository coverage.
Rename the tool to "grep_symbols" so the agent associates it with the Grep behavior it already selects reliably.

questions.question: A developer defines "codebase-explorer" and "boilerplate-writer" subagents with "AgentDefinition" and sets the coordinator's "allowedTools" to Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash. In unattended runs where unlisted tools are denied, the coordinator never delegates and explores everything itself. What change enables delegation?

options.text: Register each subagent as an MCP server in ".mcp.json" so it appears in the coordinator's tool list.
Add "Task" (named "Agent" in current SDK versions) to the coordinator's "allowedTools" list.
Add "Task" to each subagent's "tools" field so the subagents can accept delegated work.
Rewrite the coordinator's system prompt to explicitly instruct it to delegate exploration to the subagents.

questions.question: A PreToolUse hook matching the agent's migration tool denies every call, enforcing the rule that production migrations must be handed to a DBA. The tool's "target" argument chooses between production and staging, and staging migrations are now blocked too. How should the hook be corrected?

options.text: Remove the hook and add a project CLAUDE.md rule stating that the migration tool may only be called with a staging or development target, never production.
Change the hook to run asynchronously so it records production attempts for later audit while staging and development migrations proceed without interruption.
Keep the matcher on the migration tool and inspect the "target" value in "tool_input", denying with a reason that names the DBA handoff only when the target is production.
Replace the matcher with a pattern that includes the environment, such as "mcp__dbops__run_migration:production", so the hook fires only on production calls and ignores staging.

questions.question: An engineer paused a session last week after the agent mapped a legacy module's dependencies with Read and Grep. A teammate has since merged a refactor that moved and renamed many of those files. How should the engineer continue the work?

options.text: Start a new session, injecting a structured summary of the prior findings and the list of changed files.
Resume the saved session and instruct the agent to ignore any earlier tool results that look outdated.
Resume the saved session by its session ID so the full history of earlier Read and Grep results is restored.
Resume the saved session and run compaction first so the old tool outputs are condensed before continuing.

questions.question: The main agent in this system has spent twenty turns reading a legacy billing module and now delegates a dependency-tracing subtask to a standard (non-fork) subagent. Which TWO steps make the delegation work correctly? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Plan for the main agent to read the subagent's raw Grep and Read results from the subagent's conversation later.
Require the subagent to list the file paths and call chains it found in its final report.
Include the relevant findings from the twenty prior turns directly in the subagent's delegation prompt.
Skip restating coordinator conventions for the subagent, relying on it inheriting the main agent's system prompt.

Return an error flagged retryable for both cases so the agent always retries once more before concluding the symbol is unused.

questions.question: The coordinator in this system delegates legacy-codebase exploration with a prompt that lists exact steps: glob src for every file, grep each import, then read files in order. On repositories with unusual layouts, subagents follow the script literally and miss the real architecture. How should the coordinator prompt be revised?

options.text: Have the coordinator rerun the same instructions whenever a subagent's summary comes back incomplete.
Add numbered steps covering each new repository layout so the procedure handles every structure encountered so far.
Describe the exploration goal and quality criteria, letting each subagent choose its own investigation path.
Raise each subagent's turn and context budget so it can finish the scripted procedure on larger repositories.

questions.question: A team adds ".claude/rules/terraform.md" whose YAML frontmatter sets "paths: ["terraform/**/*"]". In a fresh session, before any file is opened, Claude does not apply the Terraform conventions when asked about them. The team wants these conventions available from the first message. What should they do?

options.text: Change the glob to "../../terraform/**/*" so it resolves relative to the rule file's location.
Add a line to the rule marking the conventions as IMPORTANT so Claude prioritizes them.
Rewrite the "paths" value as a comma-separated string instead of a YAML list so it parses.
Remove the "paths" frontmatter from the rule so it loads unconditionally at session start.

questions.question: An engineer asks the agent to map every cross-module dependency in a legacy monolith before a refactor. Grep and Read results flood the main conversation, and the context is nearly exhausted before the design discussion even begins. How should the discovery phase be run?

options.text: Run /compact repeatedly during the discovery phase so the accumulated search output gets summarized as it grows.
Delegate the discovery phase to the Explore subagent and bring only its summary into the main conversation.
Move the investigation into plan mode so the read-only exploration generates less output.
Start a fresh session for each module and carry the findings forward by hand between sessions.

questions.question: A developer on this team has fallen into the habit of starting every Claude Code task in plan mode. The next task is renaming a misspelled helper function that is defined and called within a single file. How should the developer handle this task?

options.text: Fork the session into two branches so alternative names can be compared before committing.
Delegate the rename to an Explore subagent so its search output stays out of the main context.
Enter plan mode so Claude maps every reference before proposing the rename for approval.
Execute the rename directly, since the change is fully scoped and needs no exploration first.

questions.question: In about 8% of runs the coordinator spawns the report-generation subagent before the synthesis subagent has returned its cited findings, despite a system prompt instruction requiring synthesis first, so those reports ship without citations. What change guarantees the required ordering?

options.text: Have the report-generation subagent rate its confidence that citations are complete before returning.
Add few-shot examples to the coordinator prompt showing synthesis completing before report generation.
Add a "PreToolUse" hook that rejects "Task" calls to the report generator until synthesis output exists.
Rewrite the ordering instruction in bold at the top of the coordinator's system prompt.

questions.question: Logs show the coordinator spawns the document analysis subagent on nearly every request, including web-only questions with no supplied documents. That subagent's description reads "Analyzes content and extracts key findings." What change most directly fixes the unnecessary delegation?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the coordinator to avoid spawning subagents it does not need.
Rewrite the subagent's description to state it applies only when source documents are supplied.
Restrict the document analysis subagent's tools to Read and Grep so unnecessary runs cost less.
Hard-code the pipeline so the document analysis subagent always runs after web search completes.

questions.question: The team's licensing agreement forbids retrieving content from a fixed list of restricted domains. All subagents retrieve web content solely through one fetch tool, and every subagent prompt states the rule, yet audits still find restricted-domain fetches in about 3% of research runs. What change guarantees compliance?

options.text: Have the synthesis subagent rate its confidence that each source is permitted and drop uncertain ones.
Register a "PreToolUse" hook on the fetch tool that denies any call targeting a restricted domain.
