Move the restricted-domain list to the top of every subagent prompt and mark it as mandatory.
Add a "PostToolUse" hook that logs any fetch from a restricted domain for later audit review.

questions.question: Human reviewers spot-check the final reports and find that every citation names only a document title, so verifying one claim from a 200-page filing means reading the entire document. Reviewers are rejecting reports they cannot verify. What change makes each claim verifiable?

options.text: Instruct the report generator to append the most plausible page number beside each document title it cites.
Have the coordinator re-run the document analysis subagent to locate a passage whenever a reviewer questions a citation.
Require the document analysis subagent to return each finding with a quoted excerpt and its page or section location.
Pass the full text of every source document into the synthesis subagent's context so it can cite exact pages.

questions.question: In this system, the document analysis subagent's search completed successfully but found zero matching passages. The coordinator re-ran the same query three times and then labeled the topic "source unavailable" in the report. How should the coordinator handle a successful subagent result that contains no matches?

options.text: Retry the same query with exponential backoff, since zero findings usually signals a transient backend access problem.
Suppress the empty result and have the synthesis agent exclude that topic so the report contains only supported sections.
Treat the empty result as a confirmed finding, then either broaden the query or annotate the coverage gap in the report.
Ask the subagent to rate its confidence that the corpus truly contains nothing, and retry whenever that confidence is low.

questions.question: Reports from the system described above sometimes come out incomplete, and the team cannot tell what the synthesis subagent actually received. A developer proposes giving the document analysis subagent a peer-messaging tool so it hands findings straight to synthesis. Which design should the team adopt?

options.text: Keep the coordinator as the only relay, passing each subagent's final report into the synthesis prompt.
Merge document analysis and synthesis into one subagent so no inter-agent handoff is needed.
Grant the peer-messaging tool, but have each subagent append every message it sends to a shared log file.
Grant the peer-messaging tool and have the coordinator receive only the synthesis subagent's final report.

questions.question: The team wrote a custom Messages API loop for the report-generation subagent that ends when the assistant text contains the phrase "Final report complete". Some runs stop after a mid-task section summary uses that phrase. What should determine loop termination instead?

options.text: Require a more distinctive sentinel phrase in the system prompt and match it with a stricter regular expression.
Stop the loop as soon as any response includes a text block alongside its tool calls.
Continue the loop while "stop_reason" is "tool_use" and stop when the response returns "end_turn".
Cap the loop at a fixed number of iterations and treat reaching the cap as the completion signal.

questions.question: Asked to find every code path in this system's codebase that performs a web search, Claude Code Greps for "SearchClient.search" and gets a single match inside a wrapper function named "run_search" in "search/wrapper.py". What should it do next?

options.text: Report that web search happens in exactly one place, since Grep returned only one match.
Read every file under "agents/" so no caller of the search client is missed.
Spawn a subagent for each top-level directory to search for callers in parallel.
Grep for "run_search" to find the wrapper's callers, then Read those files to continue the trace.

questions.question: The report generator subagent needs to fix one citation block in a generated Markdown report. Edit fails because the block appears in five identical sections, and even when the match text is extended with surrounding lines, it still matches more than once. What should the subagent do next?

options.text: Call Edit again with "replace_all" set to true so the uniqueness requirement no longer applies.
Retry the identical Edit call a few times with backoff in case the match failure is transient.
Switch to Bash and patch the targeted lines in the report with a sed command.
Read the full file, apply the change within that content, then Write the complete updated file.

questions.question: The web search subagent returns 25 sources. The coordinator then invokes the document analysis subagent (a standard subagent, not a fork) with the prompt "analyze the documents found in the previous step," and the analysis subagent replies that no documents were provided. How should the coordinator fix this handoff?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the analysis subagent to review the coordinator's earlier tool results before starting.
Retry the delegation with firmer wording insisting the subagent locate the documents identified in the previous phase.
Set the search findings as the analysis subagent's "initialPrompt" in its definition so they load automatically on invocation.
Summarize the search phase findings and include the source list in the delegation prompt that spawns the analysis subagent.

questions.question: A developer paused an Agent SDK session in which the agent had mapped how the synthesis subagent assembles citations. Most of those source files have since been refactored. Which TWO approaches keep the continued work from relying on stale analysis? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Resume the session and have the agent rate its confidence in the earlier analysis before continuing the work.
Register a "SessionStart" hook that injects the list of recently changed files into the agent's context on resume.
Resume the session unchanged, because the agent's earlier file reads are refreshed automatically from disk when it loads.
Start a new session seeded with a structured summary of prior findings and a note of which files were refactored.

questions.question: In this system, the synthesis subagent has an MCP tool "query_findings" that returns findings with source attribution from the shared store, but its description reads only "Queries findings" and documents no parameters. The subagent instead Greps the raw scratchpad files. Which TWO changes most directly fix this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a blanket system prompt rule telling the subagent to always prefer MCP tools over built-in tools.
Reorder the tool definitions so the MCP tool appears before Grep in the list sent to the model.
Drop Grep from the synthesis subagent's tool list so only role-relevant tools remain available.
Expand the description with the query parameter's expected format and example queries the tool should handle.

questions.question: The coordinator chooses between two summarizing tools: "summarize_source", run by the web-search agent, and "summarize_document", run by the document agent. Both tools have the description "summarizes a source and returns key points." Requests to summarize uploaded whitepapers often go to "summarize_source". Which TWO changes most directly resolve the misrouting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add few-shot routing examples to the coordinator prompt showing uploads going to the document agent.
Insert a pre-routing classifier that inspects each request for file references before the coordinator delegates.
Rename the web-search agent's tool to "summarize_web_page" so its name no longer mirrors the document tool.
Rewrite both descriptions to state when each applies, such as fetched URLs versus uploaded files.

questions.question: Research runs take several hours. When the coordinator process crashes midway, the restarted run repeats web searches that had already finished and discards partial document analysis. Which design lets the coordinator pick up where the run stopped?

options.text: Wrap the entire pipeline in an automatic retry with backoff so a crashed run restarts itself from the beginning without operator action.
Resume the coordinator's saved session on restart so that every subagent automatically continues from the last tool result that it had recorded.
Give each subagent a larger context budget so a single long-running pass finishes the entire pipeline before any crash can interrupt it.
Export each subagent's structured state to a known location, and load it as a manifest the coordinator feeds into subsequent subagent prompts.

questions.question: Reports from the system described above on broad topics such as "autonomous vehicle regulation" consistently cover only United States federal rules; coordinator logs show it assigned three subtasks, all within that one area. Which change most directly fixes this coverage gap?

options.text: Instruct the synthesis subagent to write additional sections for any regions the gathered findings omit.
Revise the coordinator prompt to map the topic's full scope into distinct subtasks before delegating.
Raise the web search subagent's result limit so each assigned query returns more sources.
Move the synthesis subagent to a larger context window so it can retain every finding.

questions.question: The extraction agent calls a vendor lookup tool for every invoice in a session; each call returns more than 40 fields, but extraction needs only three. Accuracy drops by the twelfth invoice. Which TWO changes address this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the model to disregard any vendor fields that are not relevant to the extraction.
Trim the vendor lookup response to only the fields the extraction step actually uses before it enters context.
Enable server-side context editing so older tool results are cleared once a configured token threshold is exceeded.
Mark the vendor lookup results with "cache_control" so the repeated fields stop counting against the context window.

questions.question: In this system, the extraction call also rates its own confidence for each field. However, fields that later turn out to be wrong get confidence above 0.9 just as often as correct fields, so almost nothing is routed to reviewers. What change makes the confidence signal usable for routing?

options.text: Ask the extraction call to critique its own draft output and revise each confidence value before returning the result.
Run the extraction three times and average the three confidence values reported for each field.
Run a separate verification pass in a fresh instance that checks each field against the source and assigns confidence.
Lower the routing threshold so that any field below 0.95 confidence is sent to a human reviewer.

questions.question: This team sets "tool_choice" to force "extract_metadata" on the first request, then returns its "tool_result". Every follow-up response calls "extract_metadata" again, and the enrichment tools never run. The request configuration is identical on every turn. What change fixes this while keeping extraction guaranteed first?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling Claude to move on to enrichment once metadata exists.
Retry the follow-up request with error feedback whenever no enrichment tool is called.
Switch every request, including the first, to "tool_choice" set to "any" instead.
Set "tool_choice" back to "auto" on the follow-up requests that carry the extraction result.

questions.question: After moving invoice extraction to a tool with an "input_schema", parse failures disappeared, yet finance still finds totals that do not match the line items and vendor names placed in the customer field. What should the team add?

options.text: Validate each extraction in code against business rules like reconciling totals, then retry with the specific error.
Mark every field in the input schema as required so the model cannot leave the total unresolved.
Set "strict: true" on the extraction tool definition so the input schema is enforced during sampling.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the model to re-check its arithmetic and field placement before calling the tool.

questions.question: A team's contract extraction tool is defined with "strict" set to true, and its "input_schema" currently marks every field as a required string. When a contract contains no termination clause, the returned "tool_use" input still includes a plausible termination date that appears nowhere in the source document. What change best prevents this?

options.text: Add a validation-retry loop that sends the suspicious date back to the model with an error message asking it to recheck.
Declare the termination date field as nullable so the model can legitimately return null when the clause is absent.
Add a required confidence score field next to the date so downstream systems can discard values the model rates as low confidence.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the model never to invent a date that the document does not explicitly state.

questions.question: The team's labeled validation set shows 97% overall extraction accuracy, and leadership wants to stop routing every extraction to human review. What should the team do before reducing review coverage?

options.text: Audit a small uniformly random sample of production extractions since the overall accuracy is already high.
Enable strict schema validation so any output that fails the JSON schema is automatically routed to review.
Break the validation results down by document type and by field to confirm accuracy holds in every segment.
Have the model rate its own confidence for each document and skip review whenever it reports high confidence.

questions.question: The system extracts entire twelve-document loan packets in one call. Some documents yield detailed fields, others almost none, and the applicant's income comes back with conflicting values across documents. How should the extraction be restructured?

options.text: Extract each document in a focused pass, then run a separate pass reconciling values across documents.
Switch to a model with a larger context window so the entire packet is processed comfortably in one pass.
Add a validation-retry loop that sends schema validation errors back to the model for self-correction.
Run the full-packet extraction three times and keep only values that match in at least two runs.

questions.question: The team's invoice extraction tool already has an "input_schema", and every result is validated in code afterward. The schema declares amounts as numbers, "line_items" as an array, and "vendor_name" as required. They plan to set "strict" to true on the tool and delete that validation step. Which check must still be kept in application code?

options.text: Keep a code check that flags invoice and due dates swapped between their two fields.
Keep a code check that flags the line_items array arriving as a single object instead.
Keep a code check that flags the required vendor_name field being missing from the tool call input.
Keep a code check that flags monetary amounts arriving as strings such as "42.10".

questions.question: The extraction tool uses a strict JSON schema, and the source documents write percentages and amounts in different styles (for example "5%" or "0.05", "$1,200" or "1200 USD"). A developer proposes handling this entirely through "minimum" and "maximum" schema keywords. Which TWO approaches should the team use instead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Mark the percentage and currency fields as required in the schema so the model is forced into the standard form.
Add "minimum" and "maximum" keywords to the schema so the API rejects any value outside the expected range.
Validate parsed values in code afterward, because a schema-conformant response can still contain un-normalized numbers.
Write the percentage and currency normalization rules into the prompt or field descriptions rather than schema keywords.

questions.question: Audits show that when a receipt contains no purchase order number, the extraction still returns a plausible-looking one; the tool schema lists "purchase_order_number" as a required string. What change best prevents these fabricated values?

options.text: Add a self-rated confidence score next to each required field so downstream code can discard low-confidence values.
Make the fields that may be missing nullable in the schema and instruct Claude to return null when a document lacks them.
Keep every field required and add a system prompt instruction forbidding Claude from inventing values it cannot find.
Keep the schema unchanged and add a validation-retry loop that sends the fabricated value back with the original document.

questions.question: When the system finds conflicting values, it outputs a discrepancy flag. Every flag passes schema validation, but the flag content varies: "location" is sometimes a page reference and sometimes a paraphrase, and "suggested_resolution" ranges from a concrete correction to "verify this". Detailed field descriptions in the prompt have not helped. What change most reliably produces consistent flags?

options.text: Retry each extraction up to three times and keep the response whose flags look most complete.
Ask the model to rate its confidence in each flag so downstream steps can discard vaguely written ones.
Rewrite the field descriptions with stronger wording that every flag must follow the specification exactly.
Add two to four few-shot examples of complete flags showing the exact expected content for each field.

questions.question: The system submitted 5,000 documents as one overnight batch. Results show 4,900 succeeded, while 100 errored with "invalid_request_error" because those documents exceeded the model's context limit. What is the best way to recover the failed extractions?

options.text: Retry only the failed documents through synchronous calls with a larger "max_tokens" value so they fit.
Locate the failed documents by their line position in the results file and resubmit them unchanged.
Collect the errored "custom_id" values, split those documents into chunks, and submit only them in a new batch.
Resubmit the entire original batch unchanged so the failed documents get another processing attempt.

questions.question: A team extracts each 18-section application bundle in a single request, using a forced extraction tool and explicit normalization rules. Bank statements early in a bundle are extracted thoroughly, while identical statements near the end come back sparse and unnormalized, yet every output validates against the schema. How should the team restructure the extraction?

options.text: Rewrite the normalization rules in stronger, more emphatic wording so the model applies them to every section.
Extract each section in its own focused pass, then run a separate integration pass for cross-section checks.
Raise "max_tokens" so the model has enough output budget to fully extract the final sections of the bundle.
Make every field in the schema required so the model cannot return sparse data for the later sections.

questions.question: The pipeline retries failed extractions by sending back the document, the prior output, and the validation error. For invoices that contain no purchase order number, every retry returns a different plausible-looking number. What change best fixes this?

options.text: Make the field nullable and route documents that lack the value to a separate handling path.
Define the extraction as a tool with the field marked required so the model must populate it.
Run the extraction three times for these invoices and keep the number that appears most often.
Raise the retry limit from two to five attempts so the model has more chances to correct itself.

questions.question: A developer must rebuild the pipeline's test-generation harness, a change touching more than 40 files with several viable integration strategies and unclear dependencies. How should the developer begin this work in Claude Code?

options.text: Start in direct execution and switch to plan mode only when the work becomes complicated.
Start in plan mode to explore the codebase and approve a plan before edits begin.
Execute immediately and run /compact regularly so the growing context never derails the work.
Begin direct execution with detailed upfront instructions that specify every file change in advance.

questions.question: To cut API costs, this team moved both its nightly test generation and its blocking pull request review step to the Message Batches API. Developers now sometimes wait hours for review feedback before they can merge. What should the team change?

options.text: Move both workflows back to synchronous calls to keep one consistent API pattern.
Poll the batch status more frequently so review results are retrieved the moment processing finishes.
Return the pull request review step to synchronous calls and keep nightly test generation on batches.
Submit each pull request review as its own single-request batch so smaller batches complete sooner.

questions.question: The pipeline extracts acceptance criteria from design documents in pull requests. Some documents state criteria inline in narrative prose; others use structured requirements tables. Despite detailed instructions covering both formats, extraction remains inconsistent. What change most reliably improves consistency?

options.text: Add a few-shot example of correct extraction from each document structure, with brief reasoning.
Run the extraction three times per document and keep the output produced by the majority.
Require teams to rewrite design documents into one standard template before extraction runs.
Expand the instructions with more detailed written rules describing each document structure explicitly.

questions.question: The reviewer currently posts every finding as a blocking pull request comment, and developers complain that uncertain findings waste their time. The team wants confident findings posted directly while uncertain ones go to a human triage queue. How should they implement this routing?

options.text: Instruct the reviewer to report only high-confidence findings so every posted comment can safely be blocking.
Map each finding's severity label to a route, treating critical and high severity as confident enough to post directly.
Run the review pass twice and send to triage any finding that appears in only one of the two runs.
Have the reviewer attach a confidence level to each finding and route on a threshold calibrated against labeled findings.

questions.question: A nightly batch job submits one code review request per changed file and maps the Nth line of the results file to the Nth submitted request. Reviews occasionally attach to the wrong files. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Submit the per-file requests in sorted order so the results file comes back in that same sequence.
Embed the file path in each prompt and parse it back out of the model's generated review text.
Match each result to its originating request using the "custom_id" field instead of line position.
Detect misaligned results after each run and automatically resubmit the whole batch until they align.

questions.question: One job in the pipeline defines two tools, "report_review_findings" and "suggest_test_cases", but its downstream parser accepts exactly one review-findings tool call per run. Some runs instead return test suggestions, plain prose, or multiple parallel tool calls. Which configuration guarantees the parser always receives a single review-findings call?

options.text: Set "tool_choice" to {"type": "tool", "name": "report_review_findings"} and set "disable_parallel_tool_use" to true.
Set "tool_choice" to {"type": "any"} with "disable_parallel_tool_use" set to true so exactly one tool is called each run.
Keep "tool_choice" at {"type": "auto"} and strengthen the system prompt to always call the review findings tool first.
Enable "strict": true on the review findings tool so schema enforcement guarantees that tool is the one invoked.

questions.question: The pipeline extracts review findings into a tool schema that marks "related_ticket" as required, and Claude invents plausible ticket IDs whenever a pull request description references no ticket. What schema change most reliably prevents these fabricated values?

options.text: Change "related_ticket" to a nullable type so Claude can return null when no ticket is referenced.
Validate each extracted ticket ID against the issue tracker and retry the extraction when validation fails.
Add a system prompt instruction stating that ticket identifiers must never be guessed or invented.
Have Claude attach a confidence score to each ticket ID so low-confidence values can be filtered out.

questions.question: A nightly audit step uses Claude to extract vulnerability counts from scanner reports into JSON, which decides whether a pull request can be merged. Some reports contain a summary line whose total disagrees with the list of individual findings, and the extraction silently returns a single value. How should the extraction be redesigned?

options.text: Instruct the model in the prompt to report whichever of the conflicting counts it judges more reliable.
Add a validation retry loop that re-prompts the model with the error until the two counts in its output agree.
Extract both the stated total and a total computed from the listed entries, with a boolean flagging mismatches.
Add a numeric constraint to the JSON schema requiring the total field to equal the sum of the listed entries.

questions.question: Metrics show an automated code reviewer's performance findings are wrong about half the time, while its security findings are over 90% accurate. Developers have begun dismissing findings across all categories without reading them. What should the team do?

options.text: Attach the model's self-rated confidence score to each finding so developers can judge which ones to investigate.
Temporarily disable the performance category while its prompts are improved, keeping the accurate categories live.
Make the reviewer less strict in every category to lower the overall false-positive rate.
Keep every category live and rely on the category labels so developers can discount performance findings selectively.

questions.question: The pipeline extracts structured ticket metadata from each pull request description, validates the result against a JSON schema, and retries failures with the validation error attached. Which TWO statements about this retry loop are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Sending back the specific validation error typically fixes format and structural mistakes within a retry or two.
Raising the retry limit from two attempts to five eventually recovers values that are missing from the source.
Having the model rate its own confidence on each retry resolves persistent validation failures.
No number of retries can produce a value that is simply absent from the submitted PR description.

questions.question: A review-summary extraction step uses a validation-retry loop, and most failures resolve within two retries. One required field, the linked ticket's acceptance criteria, fails on every retry because that information exists only in the issue tracker, not in the pull request diff sent to Claude. What change resolves this failure class?

options.text: Strengthen the prompt to state that the acceptance criteria field is mandatory and must never be empty.
Have Claude self-rate confidence per field and accept its lowest-confidence guess after the final retry.
Raise the retry limit from two to five and include fuller validation errors on each attempt.
Include the ticket's acceptance criteria from the issue tracker in the request context before extraction.

questions.question: You are writing a SKILL.md for a skill that finds missing tests in CI and produces thousands of lines of exploratory output. Which two implementation choices should you make? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Write all context the task needs into the skill itself, since a forked skill starts with no history.
Set "context: fork" in the frontmatter so the verbose exploration runs in an isolated subagent.
Keep the skill brief and rely on the fork inheriting the session's prior messages for task details.
Omit "allowed-tools" because "context: fork" already restricts the subagent to read-only operations.

questions.question: The team plans to use the Message Batches API overnight to generate test-case suggestions for 8,000 legacy modules, using a newly written prompt that has never been run at scale. What should they do before submitting the full batch?

options.text: Rewrite the prompt with stronger, more emphatic instructions about accuracy before launching the full batch.
Run the prompt synchronously on a representative sample of modules, iterating until outputs meet quality criteria.
Submit the entire batch now and use "custom_id" values to identify and resubmit any requests that fail.
Add an automated retry loop that resubmits each unsatisfactory batch result with its validation error attached.

questions.question: A team's Agent SDK tool generates refactoring changes across a service, then runs an automated review step before opening a pull request. The review must not be influenced by the reasoning that produced the changes. How should the reviewer be set up?

options.text: Delegate to a standard subagent, passing the diff, affected files, and review criteria in its prompt.
Have the generating agent attach a confidence score to each change and show reviewers only the low-confidence ones.
Fork the generating session so the reviewer starts with the files and decisions already in context.
Resume the generating agent and instruct it to critique its own changes against the review criteria.

questions.question: During a multi-phase refactoring task, the team spawns investigation subagents, but each one returns full file contents plus its step-by-step reasoning, rapidly consuming the main conversation's context window. What change addresses this most effectively?

options.text: Instruct the main agent in CLAUDE.md to disregard irrelevant detail when reading subagent reports.
Have each subagent return structured findings: key facts, file paths, and relevance, not raw content.
Switch the main conversation to a model with a larger context window and keep accumulating reports.
Run /compact after each subagent completes so its verbose report is summarized before the next one starts.

questions.question: A developer gave Claude Code three input/output test cases while asking it to implement a date-normalization function. The generated code contains branches matching those exact inputs and fails on other valid date formats. What prompt change most effectively fixes this?

options.text: Replace the test cases with a detailed prose description of the normalization rules.
Have Claude rate its confidence for each supported input format and retry the low-confidence conversions.
Ask for a general-purpose solution that treats the test cases as verification, not the full specification.
Add another example to the prompt each time a new failing input appears in production.

questions.question: Your monorepo has a packages/mobile/ directory whose coding conventions differ from the rest of the codebase. Teammates should receive these conventions automatically whenever they work on mobile files, without the conventions loading into unrelated sessions. Where should the conventions live?

options.text: In each developer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, with a note to apply them only to mobile code.
In a skill under .claude/skills/ that developers invoke before editing mobile code.
In a CLAUDE.md file inside packages/mobile/, committed to the repository.
In a clearly labeled section of the root CLAUDE.md so every session can see them.

questions.question: Developers notice that when they ask Claude Code to generate tests, the output is mostly trivial assertions and hand-built mock data that ignores the team's shared fixture factories. What change most improves the quality of generated tests?

options.text: Have each developer copy the testing standards into their personal user-level CLAUDE.md file.
Add a sentence to each generation prompt telling Claude to write thorough, meaningful, high-quality tests.
Ask Claude to rate the value of each generated test and discard low-rated ones automatically.
Document testing standards, criteria for valuable tests, and available fixtures in the project CLAUDE.md.

questions.question: A developer committed their personal style preferences to the project root CLAUDE.md, and every teammate's sessions now follow them. The developer wants these preferences active in all of their own projects while affecting no one else. Where should the preferences live?

options.text: In a clearly labeled personal section of the project CLAUDE.md that teammates ignore.
In "~/.claude/settings.json", saved as personal preference settings on that machine.
In "CLAUDE.local.md" at the repository root, with the file added to ".gitignore".
In "~/.claude/CLAUDE.md", which applies only to that user across all projects.

questions.question: During a multi-day refactoring session, the team relies on /compact several times. Afterward, Claude quotes incorrect dependency version pins and migration dates it had read correctly earlier. Which TWO practices address this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have Claude re-read the relevant source files to verify exact values before quoting them in responses.
Run /compact proactively after every few turns so the summary is regenerated from fresher context.
Record exact values such as version pins and migration dates in a scratchpad file Claude rereads later.
Ask Claude to attach a confidence rating to each quoted value and accept only high-rated ones.

questions.question: To cut review load, the team has Claude self-rate each generated change on a 1 to 10 confidence scale, auto-approving anything rated 8 or higher. Several highly rated changes still shipped subtle bugs. What explains this failure?

options.text: The rating is returned as free text rather than structured JSON, so the pipeline misreads the values.
The 1-to-10 scale is too coarse; a percentage scale would separate safe changes from risky ones more cleanly.
Self-rated confidence is poorly calibrated; the model is often confidently wrong on the hardest cases.
Confidence ratings degrade as session context fills up; running /compact before each rating would restore accuracy.

questions.question: Midway through coordinating a large refactor, you need to answer one focused question: which modules still call a deprecated payment helper. Grepping and reading dozens of files would fill the main session's context with verbose output. What is the best approach?

options.text: Run /compact after each batch of file reads so the main conversation stays within its limits.
Record the candidate file list in CLAUDE.md so the findings persist and reload in every session.
Spawn a subagent to run the investigation and return only a concise summary of the call sites.
Switch the main session to a model with a larger context window and read the files directly.

questions.question: Your project CLAUDE.md has grown to 600 lines, mixing universal coding standards with testing conventions that apply only to test files scattered across the codebase. Which two actions best reorganize this configuration? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep the universal coding standards in a short project-level CLAUDE.md so they load in every session.
Move every convention into unscoped .claude/rules/ files so none of the content consumes context at launch.
Move the testing conventions into a .claude/rules/ file with a "paths" glob matching the test files.
Split the file using "@path" imports from CLAUDE.md so each imported section loads only when it is needed.

questions.question: A developer copied the team's shared /deploy skill to "~/.claude/skills/deploy-verbose/" to experiment locally, but kept "name: deploy" in the copied SKILL.md frontmatter. Now typing /deploy runs the personal copy instead of the shared project skill. What fixes this?

options.text: Run /reload-skills so Claude Code re-reads the repository's shared skill directory.
Change the "name" field in the personal copy's frontmatter to a value other than "deploy".
Set "disable-model-invocation: true" in the personal copy's SKILL.md frontmatter.
Move the personal copy into the repository's .claude/skills/ directory alongside the shared skill.

questions.question: Your team's custom MCP ticket-lookup tool returns only the string "Operation failed" whether the tracker times out or the ticket ID is invalid, so Claude retries bad IDs and gives up on timeouts that a retry would fix. What change best enables appropriate recovery?

options.text: Add a CLAUDE.md instruction to retry any failed tool call up to three times before moving on.
Return an empty result marked successful so the session continues without interruption when lookups fail.
Return the failure category and a suggested alternative in a tool result marked with "isError".
Retry the lookup inside the tool with backoff, reporting a generic unavailable status after retries are exhausted.

questions.question: An MCP tool this team added returns a JSON payload with 50+ fields on every call, though only five of them matter for the debugging workflow. During long sessions these results accumulate and response quality degrades. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Add a CLAUDE.md rule instructing Claude to disregard the irrelevant result fields.
Run /compact after every few tool calls so summaries keep the context lean.
Enable prompt caching so the repeated verbose tool results cost fewer tokens.
Change the tool to return only the fields the debugging workflow uses.

questions.question: The team is sorting its backlog by execution style. Which two tasks are good candidates for direct execution rather than plan mode? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Migrate the codebase to a new HTTP client library, touching more than 45 files.
Fix an off-by-one bug in one file, pinpointed by a clear stack trace.
Split a shared module into separate services, with several viable boundary designs to weigh.
Add a single input validation check to one function whose behavior is already understood.

questions.question: A team's CI script runs "claude -p" with "--output-format json" and a valid JSON Schema supplied via "--json-schema". A jq step reads the ".result" field but gets conversational prose instead of data matching the schema. What should the script do instead?

options.text: Wrap the command in a retry loop that reruns it until the "result" field parses as valid JSON.
Switch to "--output-format stream-json", where each event arrives as parseable JSON.
Keep reading the "result" field and add a prompt instruction telling Claude to reply with raw JSON only.
Read the "structured_output" field, where the CLI places the schema-validated data.

questions.question: The team has Claude Code generate docstrings and API reference entries across a large codebase, but technical writers can review only about one fifth of the output. How should the team decide which generated items receive human review?

options.text: Output per-item confidence scores, calibrate a review threshold on labeled data, and route low-confidence items to reviewers.
Automate approval entirely for every item, since the pipeline's measured aggregate accuracy already exceeds the team's quality bar.
Validate each generated item against a JSON schema and route only the items that fail validation to human reviewers.
Send a uniform random sample covering one fifth of the generated docstrings and reference entries to reviewers each week.

questions.question: The agent invokes the MCP tool "mcp__ci__run_tests" (called "run_tests" below) for nearly any request mentioning tests, including requests to locate test files, even though every tool description is detailed and distinct. The system prompt contains: "CRITICAL: You MUST use run_tests whenever testing is mentioned." What change most directly fixes the misrouting?

options.text: Reduce the agent's overall tool catalog so "run_tests" competes with fewer alternatives at selection time.
Expand the "run_tests" description with boundary language distinguishing executing tests from locating test files.
Replace the all-caps MUST rule with calm wording that says when tests actually need to run.
Add few-shot routing examples to the system prompt showing when Glob should be used instead of "run_tests".

questions.question: A coordinator agent delegates legacy-system investigations to subagents using a prompt that lists eight numbered tool-call steps. Investigations fail whenever a codebase's layout differs from the structure those steps assume. How should the coordinator prompt be revised?

options.text: State the investigation goal and the quality criteria the final report must meet, letting the agent choose its steps.
Expand the numbered procedure with conditional branches covering every repository layout the team expects to encounter.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks any tool call issued outside the prescribed step order.
Add few-shot examples showing the exact tool-call sequence that succeeded on one representative codebase.

questions.question: An agent endpoint uses "tool_choice" of type "any" to guarantee a tool call, but responses sometimes contain multiple parallel tool_use blocks, breaking a harness built to execute one call per turn. What change guarantees exactly one tool call per response?

options.text: Add a system prompt rule instructing Claude to emit only one tool call per response.
Set "disable_parallel_tool_use" to true inside the "tool_choice" object.
Set "strict" to true on every tool definition so the API enforces one call at a time.
Force a single named tool with "tool_choice" of type "tool" instead of the "any" type.

questions.question: A coordinator spawns an exploration subagent that maps a legacy module's conventions, then spawns a generation subagent to produce boilerplate matching those conventions. Both are ordinary subagents (not forks) with default settings. They have no shared memory and no way to message each other. How does the generation subagent obtain the exploration findings?

options.text: The generation subagent automatically inherits the coordinator's conversation history, which contains the explorer's report.
The exploration subagent delivers its findings directly to the generation subagent as soon as its own task finishes.
Both subagents read and write a shared session memory that the SDK maintains across all spawned subagents.
The coordinator includes the explorer's returned findings in the prompt it uses to spawn the generation subagent.

questions.question: A developer is designing how a main agent delegates to a documentation subagent (not a fork) that summarizes a legacy module. Which two actions make sure the subagent starts with the context it needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Put the subagent's specialized instructions in its own system prompt, since the main agent's system prompt is not carried over.
Let the subagent reuse files the main agent already read, since tool results are shared across agents within a session.
Omit prior findings from the delegation prompt, since the main agent's full conversation history is copied into the subagent automatically.
Rely on the project CLAUDE.md loading automatically for the subagent, and pass prior findings in the delegation prompt.

questions.question: Despite a system prompt rule forbidding changes to files under the migrations directory, logs show the agent occasionally modifies them during automated refactors. The team needs guaranteed prevention of these edits. What should they implement?

options.text: Move the rule to the top of the system prompt and restate it in CLAUDE.md with strong emphasis.
Add a "PostToolUse" hook that detects writes to the migrations directory and alerts the team when they occur.
Add few-shot examples to the system prompt showing the agent refusing tasks that touch migration files.
Register a "PreToolUse" hook that returns a "deny" decision for any tool call targeting the migrations directory.

questions.question: While automating a routine configuration update, the agent called Write with only the updated version constant, replacing a 2,000-line settings file with that single line. What change to the agent's tool usage prevents this data loss on future small modifications?

options.text: Add a system prompt rule stating that Write must append to existing files instead of replacing them.
Have the agent Read the file first so that Write merges the new constant into the existing contents.
Use Bash with output redirection to append the updated constant line to the end of the file.
Use Edit, passing the current constant line as "old_string" and the replacement as "new_string".

questions.question: An agent consumes several MCP tools that return inconsistent result formats (Unix timestamps, varied date strings, numeric status codes). The team is building a single PostToolUse hook that converts every tool's results to one format. Which two design decisions should they make? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Return a "decision: block" with a reason so the raw tool output is hidden and only the reason reaches the model.
Return "updatedToolOutput" from the hook so the model sees the normalized result instead of the raw output.
Use the PostToolUse hook to block calls that break the format rules so side effects such as file writes never occur.
Have the hook read "tool_name" from its input to apply the right transformation for each tool's format.

questions.question: The team wants the agent to apply strict testing conventions whenever it edits a test file. Test files sit next to the source they cover in nearly every directory, and the conventions should not occupy context during unrelated work. What should the team create?

options.text: A skill in ".claude/skills/" that packages the testing conventions as a reusable workflow.
A section in the root CLAUDE.md so the conventions are loaded into every session.
A file in ".claude/rules/" whose YAML frontmatter sets "paths" to a glob matching test files.
A CLAUDE.md file containing the testing conventions in every directory that holds test files.

questions.question: Your team shares a "/gen-boilerplate" command through the repository so everyone generates starter code the same way. One engineer reports the command ignores the team's template; the engineer has no local changes ("git status" is clean), and the committed command file matches everyone else's. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Add the command to the "permissions" allow list in ".claude/settings.json" so the project version loads on every machine.
Copy the command's template rules into the project CLAUDE.md so they load in every session regardless of command scope.
Remove or rename the engineer's identically named personal command in "~/.claude/commands/", which overrides the project version.
Have the engineer run /clear to reset the session, since accumulated conversation context is overriding the command's instructions.

questions.question: A team configures a Claude Code PreToolUse command hook that blocks Bash commands modifying files outside the repository. An audit of unattended runs shows the hook script crashed on several occasions, and the commands it should have blocked executed anyway. What change closes this gap?

options.text: Move the enforcement to a PostToolUse hook so violations are detected after each command runs.
Wrap the hook script in automatic retries so transient crashes resolve before the tool call runs.
Configure the hook with "onFailure": "block" so a hook failure denies the tool call.
Add a system prompt rule forbidding those commands so the model refuses them if the hook fails.

questions.question: The agent is asked to catalog every external integration in a legacy monolith. The coordinator delegates subtasks for REST clients, webhooks, and HTTP middleware; all three subagents finish their work correctly, yet database and message queue integrations are absent from the catalog. What is the most likely root cause?

options.text: Context isolation prevented the subagents from sharing discoveries, so findings about non-HTTP integrations were lost in handoff.
The step that assembles the final catalog lacks instructions to check its output for coverage gaps before finalizing.
The coordinator decomposed the task too narrowly, so non-HTTP integration types were never assigned to any subagent.
The subagents wrote Grep patterns that were too specific, causing them to overlook database and queue connection code.

questions.question: To stop the agent answering codebase questions from memory, the team added "CRITICAL: You MUST call a tool before responding" to its system prompt. Now it runs Grep even for follow-ups already answered in the conversation. What change makes the agent call tools only when it needs to?

options.text: Add a hook that blocks tool calls whenever the user's message falls below a length threshold.
Set "tool_choice" to "none" by default, switching to "auto" only when a message mentions code.
Reword the directive to normal guidance such as "use the tools to investigate when needed".
Expand each tool's description with boundary language stating when the tool should not be used.

questions.question: The agent must find every call site of a utility function "formatCurrency" that several wrapper modules re-export under different alias names. Which TWO steps form the correct tracing workflow? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Glob for each alias across file contents, since identifiers can be expressed as path patterns.
Grep the codebase for each exported alias to locate call sites that import through the wrappers.
Grep only for "formatCurrency", since every call path resolves to the original function name.
Read each wrapper module to identify every name under which "formatCurrency" is exported.

questions.question: An agent running an automated migration fails partway through. The agent used subagents to investigate parts of the failure, and it must now escalate to an on-call engineer who has no access to the session transcript or the subagents' sessions. Which two practices produce an effective handoff? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Compile a self-contained summary with the task identifiers, the root cause analysis so far, and a recommended next action.
Attach every raw tool output the agent collected so the engineer can inspect all underlying evidence directly.
Include subagent findings and evidence directly in the handoff instead of referencing those subagents' isolated sessions.
Send only the task identifier and failure category so the engineer forms an independent diagnosis without being influenced by the agent's analysis.

questions.question: A teammate proposes that the codebase-exploration subagent should hand its findings straight to the boilerplate-generation subagent, skipping the coordinator to reduce round trips. Which design preserves observability and controlled information flow?

options.text: Grant both subagents a peer-messaging tool so the explorer can send its findings directly to the generator.
Have each subagent report back to the coordinator, which includes the relevant findings in the next subagent's prompt.
Have both subagents write to and read from a shared scratchpad file to exchange intermediate results.
Give the generator subagent the same repository tools and have it re-run the exploration itself before generating.

questions.question: A research subagent's "fetch_report" MCP tool reports failures with "isError": true plus two custom fields the team added, "errorCategory" and "isRetryable". When the archive denies access to a source outside the team's subscription, the tool returns "errorCategory": "transient" with "isRetryable": true, so the subagent keeps retrying the same call until it runs out of attempts. Which change fixes the recovery behavior?

options.text: Return the denial as a permission error with "isRetryable": false so the subagent escalates instead of retrying.
Add exponential backoff between successive retry attempts so the repeated calls place less load on the archive service.
Have the tool catch the denial and return an empty result marked as successful so no retries are triggered.
Add a system prompt rule telling the subagent to stop retrying any tool call that fails twice in a row.

questions.question: A multi-agent research system defines each subagent programmatically with an AgentDefinition, and every subagent currently inherits the full tool catalog. Logs show the report-writing subagent updating issue-tracker records and the document-analysis subagent running broad web research. Which change restricts each subagent to only the tools its role needs?

options.text: Set each subagent's "tools" field in its AgentDefinition to its role-relevant tools, leaving unrelated tools out of its session.
Add a rule to each subagent's system prompt naming the tools outside its role that it must never call.
List each role's tool names in the session-level "allowedTools" setting so those tools are pre-approved for the subagents.
Rewrite every tool description to state which subagent role it belongs to, keeping the full catalog available.

questions.question: The synthesis agent receives roughly 80K tokens of aggregated subagent findings in a single prompt. Evaluation shows it reliably uses material from the opening and closing sections but regularly overlooks relevant findings in the middle. How should you restructure this input?

options.text: Compress every subagent's output into a short summary so the combined input stays under 20K tokens.
Place a key-findings summary at the top of the input and label detailed sections with explicit headings.
Rotate which subagent's findings appear first on each run so every source gets top placement over time.
Add a system prompt instruction directing the synthesis agent to weigh all sections of the input equally.

questions.question: A client requests research that requires pulling content from a login-protected third-party website. The team's source-usage policy covers public web sources and the licensed internal repository, but does not mention login-protected websites. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Have the coordinator rate its confidence that access is allowed and proceed when confidence is high.
Proceed by applying the licensed-repository rules to the website, since the cases are very similar.
Escalate the request to a human operator, flagging that the source-usage policy does not address it.
Decline the request, informing the client that accessing login-protected third-party websites is against policy.

questions.question: The team needs two new backend integrations: Jira for tracking research assignments, and a proprietary internal paper archive that has no published connector. Which TWO integration decisions follow recommended practice? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Build custom MCP servers for both systems so the team maintains one unified codebase.
Build a custom MCP server only for the proprietary paper archive.
Have the agents call the Jira REST API directly through the Bash tool instead of MCP.
Connect Jira through an existing community MCP server instead of writing one from scratch.

questions.question: While implementing the agent loop for the web search subagent, a single response arrives containing two "tool_use" blocks for independent queries. Which two requirements apply when sending the tool outputs back to Claude? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Send all the "tool_result" blocks together in one user message immediately following the assistant message with the calls.
If one query fails, omit its "tool_result" block and describe the failure in plain text at the start of the next message.
Execute the two tools strictly in the order their "tool_use" blocks appear, since the API requires sequential completion.
Return each output in a "tool_result" block whose "tool_use_id" matches the "id" of its originating "tool_use" block.

questions.question: The report generation subagent's output sometimes contains uncited claims and formatting that violates the report template. The team wants these defects caught and corrected before delivery, and wants to log exactly where quality failures occur. What should they implement?

options.text: Strengthen the report subagent's system prompt with explicit instructions to verify every citation before finalizing its output.
Have the report subagent self-rate its confidence in each claim and flag any low-confidence sections for review in the final report.
Raise the report subagent's output token limit so a single pass has enough room for a more thorough report.
Chain the report stage into sequential calls: generate a draft, review it against citation and format criteria, then refine it.

questions.question: One session now holds a completed evaluation of 30 sources. The team wants to draft two different versions of the report, each building on that evaluation but with neither seeing the other's work. How should they set this up?

options.text: Resume the session twice with "fork_session" enabled, giving each version its own branched copy.
Instruct the agent in the same session to ignore the first version before producing the second.
Resume the session by its ID for each version, since resuming restores the evaluation context.
Start two fresh sessions and paste a condensed summary of the source evaluation into each one.

questions.question: The team uses the coordinator to review a 16-file pull request to its own code, all in one pass. Review depth varies widely by file, and a pattern flagged in one file is approved in another. Which two changes address the root cause? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Repeat the single-pass review three times and keep only findings reported in at least two of the runs.
Switch the review to a model with a larger context window so all 16 files receive equal attention in one pass.
Have the coordinator spawn a subagent per file for self-contained local analysis, each returning a findings summary.
Run a separate integration pass over the per-file summaries to catch cross-file issues such as inconsistent data flow.

questions.question: The team defines a shared MCP server for the web-search subagent in ".mcp.json" at the project root, checked into version control. The server needs a search provider API key. How should the team manage this credential?

options.text: Record the key in the project CLAUDE.md so Claude Code loads it automatically into every session's context.
Move the search server definition into each developer's personal "~/.claude.json" file so everyone stores their own key privately.
Use "${SEARCH_API_KEY}" in the server's "env" field in ".mcp.json", with each developer setting the variable locally.
Commit the actual key value in ".mcp.json" and rely on repository access controls to restrict who can read it.

questions.question: The system has saved its gathered sources as markdown files in a local corpus directory. The subagent's tool list explicitly includes Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash. Before citing a study, the agent must identify every file that mentions "Nakamura et al." Which tool should the agent use?

options.text: Use Bash to run a recursive shell search across the whole corpus directory.
Use Read to load each corpus file in turn and scan every one for the phrase.
Use Glob with a pattern derived from the phrase to find files whose names match it.
Use Grep to search the contents of the corpus files for that phrase.

questions.question: The coordinator frequently misroutes work: questions about uploaded documents are delegated to the web-search subagent, and simple lookups go to the synthesis subagent. Each subagent is defined programmatically with a one-line description such as "Handles research content". What change most directly fixes subagent selection?

options.text: Rewrite each subagent's description so it states distinctly what it handles and when to invoke it.
Add few-shot routing examples to the coordinator's prompt covering typical request types.
Move detailed routing rules into each subagent's system prompt so delegation decisions reflect them.
Build a pre-routing classifier that picks the subagent before the coordinator processes each request.

questions.question: The team is adding an MCP server whose tools query a hand-picked, pre-indexed collection of research documents; subagents also keep built-in Read and Grep for local files. What should each MCP tool description emphasize so subagents select these tools when appropriate?

options.text: Keep each description to a single sentence so the tool catalog consumes minimal context.
Give each tool a distinctive name, since the model selects tools primarily by their names.
State what each tool returns and the unique indexed data that built-in file tools cannot provide.
Add a coordinator prompt rule telling every subagent to always prefer MCP tools over built-in tools.

questions.question: You are deciding whether the coordinator should dynamically choose which subagents to spawn or follow a hard-coded invocation sequence (search, analyze, synthesize, report). Which two design recommendations are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Build a separate routing classifier, since the coordinator cannot select subagents on its own.
Let the coordinator choose which subagents to spawn dynamically when intermediate findings determine the next step.
Use a fixed invocation sequence when every research task follows the same stages and reproducibility matters.
Rely on model-driven delegation alone for mandatory steps, since the coordinator always invokes every required subagent.

questions.question: Different MCP tools in this system return dates as Unix timestamps, ISO 8601 strings, and plain text, and subagents sometimes misread them. Which two implementation choices correctly normalize these results before the model processes them? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Register a "PostToolUse" hook that returns "updatedToolOutput" with all dates converted to one standard format.
Describe each tool's date conventions in every subagent's system prompt so the model converts values itself.
Scope the hook with a matcher on the tools' full names in the "mcp__SERVER__TOOL" naming pattern.
Register a "PreToolUse" hook that rewrites the returned dates by setting "updatedInput" on each call.

questions.question: In the extraction pipeline, the "po_number" field fails schema validation on every attempt, even after three retries with the validation error attached. Investigation shows the value appears only in a separate purchase order document, never in the invoice being processed. What change resolves these failures?

options.text: Have the model report a confidence score for the field and accept high-confidence values.
Raise the retry limit and attach more detailed validation errors to each retry prompt.
Include the related purchase order document in the extraction request alongside the invoice.
Add a prompt instruction stating the field is mandatory and must never be left empty.

questions.question: The extraction schema's "payment_method" field uses an enum listing "credit_card", "bank_transfer", and "check". Documents increasingly mention newer payment methods, and the model forces each one into the closest listed value. Downstream analytics depend on consistent categorical values. What schema change best handles these cases?

options.text: Add an "other" enum value paired with a free-text detail field for unlisted payment methods.
Make the "payment_method" field nullable so the model can return null when no listed value fits.
Expand the enum with every payment method observed in production so far and redeploy the schema.
Replace the enum with a free-text string field so the model can record any payment method.

questions.question: The pipeline currently prefills the assistant turn with an opening brace to get JSON from the model. Downstream parsing still breaks on missing required fields, wrong data types, and occasional trailing commentary. Which change most reliably produces schema-conformant extractions?

options.text: Add a validation-retry loop that feeds parse errors back to the model until the JSON passes.
Rewrite the prompt to enumerate every required field and state that only syntactically valid JSON output is acceptable.
Define an extraction tool with the target "input_schema", set "strict" to true, and parse the "tool_use" input.
Add several few-shot examples of perfectly formatted JSON responses to the extraction prompt.

questions.question: The team's extraction prompt, used with an output schema that permits nullable fields, tells Claude to skip any field it is not confident about. On repeated runs over identical invoices, the same ambiguous fields are sometimes extracted and sometimes omitted. What change most improves consistency?

options.text: Add a retry pass that re-extracts the document whenever an ambiguous field is missing from the output.
Strengthen the instruction so Claude skips a field unless it is absolutely certain about the extracted value.
Have Claude rate its confidence for each extracted field so downstream code can filter uncertain values.
Replace the confidence instruction with explicit rules defining when a field is extracted versus returned as null.

questions.question: Despite detailed normalization rules in the prompt, documents that state quantities informally ("about two handfuls", "roughly a dozen") yield inconsistent "quantity" values across similar phrases, even though every extraction passes schema validation. What change most improves consistency?

options.text: Rewrite the normalization instructions with stronger emphasis, stating that measurements must always be normalized precisely.
Add a few targeted examples showing how informal measurements map to normalized values, with reasoning.
Tighten the schema for the quantity field with stricter type and pattern constraints to reject bad values.
Add a validation-retry loop that re-prompts Claude whenever an extracted quantity fails a format check.

questions.question: On one run, two of the five source documents used to build one summary record fail to parse. Downstream consumers complain they cannot tell which parts of the summary are actually backed by sources. How should the synthesis output be structured?

options.text: Annotate the output so well-supported findings are distinguished from topics the failed documents would have covered.
Have the model attach a single self-rated confidence score for the whole record so consumers can judge reliability.
Leave out the fields the failed documents would have populated and return the record with a success status.
Return a failure status for the whole batch and reprocess only after all five documents parse successfully.

questions.question: A teammate observes that most Message Batches finish in under an hour and proposes moving the interactive document upload flow, where users wait on-screen for extraction results, to batches for the 50% discount. How should you respond?

options.text: Move the upload path to batches but submit each upload as its own single-request batch to finish faster.
Move the upload path to batches with a synchronous fallback whenever a batch exceeds a few minutes.
Move the upload path to batches and poll batch status every few seconds to return results promptly.
Keep the interactive upload path on synchronous calls because batch completion times carry no guarantee.

questions.question: The pipeline returns schema-valid JSON for every document, but date fields arrive as "3/4/24", "March 4th", or ISO 8601 depending on the source, and amount fields sometimes include currency symbols. Downstream ingestion keeps rejecting records. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Add automatic retries that resubmit the document whenever downstream ingestion rejects a record.
Switch the extraction to a forced tool call so the output is guaranteed to conform to the schema.
Add explicit normalization rules to the prompt: dates in ISO 8601, amounts as a number plus a currency code.
Tighten the JSON schema with string pattern and length constraints that enforce standard value formats.

questions.question: The pipeline returns null for "vendor_name" on 30% of invoices, although every document contains the name. Failures cluster on invoices that list the vendor in a footer table rather than a header. Which change most effectively fixes these empty extractions?

options.text: Mark "vendor_name" as required and non-nullable in the schema so a value is always produced.
Add few-shot examples showing correct extraction from both header-based and footer-table layouts.
Add a stronger prompt instruction stating the vendor name is always present and must never be null.
Automatically resubmit the identical request whenever the extraction returns null for the field.

questions.question: An invoice extraction fails semantic validation: the extracted line items sum to 145.00 while the "stated_total" field reads 150.00. The team wants Claude to self-correct on a retry. How should the follow-up request be constructed?

options.text: Resend the identical extraction prompt up to three times and keep the first output that passes validation.
Include the original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation error about the mismatch.
Send back only the failed JSON output with an instruction to find and fix any mistakes it contains.
Add "double-check all totals before responding" to the original prompt and rerun the extraction from scratch.

questions.question: An extraction pipeline routes documents to auto-accept or human review based on the severity assigned to each validation finding. Arithmetic mismatches and harmless currency-formatting differences often receive the same severity label, so routing is unreliable. What change makes the classification dependable?

options.text: Constrain the severity field to an enum of valid labels through a tool schema so only defined values appear.
Have the model report a confidence score with each severity label and route low-confidence findings to review.
Write explicit criteria for each severity level, with a concrete example finding for each level.
Resend each finding with the original document so the model can reconsider its severity assignment.

questions.question: The team defined an "extract_invoice" tool whose "input_schema" matches the target output format, but the pipeline parses the model's response text as JSON and fails whenever Claude adds explanatory prose before the data. What change makes parsing reliable?

options.text: Add a post-processing step that strips leading prose with regular expressions before parsing.
Add a system prompt instruction forbidding any explanatory text before the JSON output.
Retry each failed request until the response text contains only the JSON object.
Parse the data from the "input" field of the "tool_use" content block in the response.

questions.question: Before each extraction run, the coordinating agent reads dozens of sample documents to identify layout variants. The raw document content fills its context, and accuracy in the later schema validation steps degrades. What change best addresses this?

options.text: Switch to a model with a larger context window and keep reading all sample documents in the main agent.
Summarize the accumulated conversation whenever the context window approaches its limit during exploration.
Delegate the layout survey to a subagent whose verbose output stays isolated, returning only a summary.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the agent to disregard raw document text once each layout is noted.

questions.question: A team's single extraction pass over long multi-section contracts produces detailed output for some sections but shallow output for others, and captures a clause type in one section while missing it in an identical section elsewhere. Which TWO changes would most effectively restore consistent extraction? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Split the extraction into focused per-section passes so each section receives full analytical depth.
Run a separate reconciliation pass that compares extracted clauses across sections to catch gaps and inconsistencies.
Rerun the full extraction pass three times and keep only values found in at least two runs.
Mark every schema field as "required" to force the model to extract each section with equal depth.

questions.question: The team exposed account operations through a single "manage_account" MCP tool that takes one free-text "instruction" parameter and interprets it server-side. Logs show frequent wrong operations: credits applied when the customer wanted an address change, and plan downgrades instead of cancellations. What redesign most directly fixes this?

options.text: Have the agent retry with a reworded instruction whenever a result looks inconsistent with the request.
Add system prompt guidance requiring the agent to write more precise and detailed instruction text.
Expand the single tool's description with example instruction phrasings the backend parser handles correctly.
Split the tool into purpose-specific tools, each with its own input schema and defined output format.

questions.question: To base policy answers on official documents, the team gave the agent a generic "fetch_url" tool for retrieving internal policy documents. Logs show the agent also fetching search results pages and third-party sites when answering return policy questions, producing inconsistent answers. Which change most reliably prevents this misuse?

options.text: Replace "fetch_url" with a "get_policy_document" tool that accepts only validated policy document identifiers.
Expand the "fetch_url" description with boundary language stating it must only retrieve internal policy document URLs.
Add a denylist inside "fetch_url" that blocks requests to known search engines and third-party domains.
Strengthen the system prompt with a rule that "fetch_url" may only be called with policy repository URLs.

questions.question: A coordinator delegates a billing dispute investigation to a subagent that reads dozens of order records and billing logs through MCP tools. The team worries this verbose output will exhaust the coordinator's context window. What should you do when designing this delegation?

options.text: Spawn the subagent without forking so its full conversation cannot merge back into the coordinator when it finishes.
Add a step that compacts the subagent's transcript into a compressed summary and inserts it into the coordinator's history.
Have the subagent forward each tool result into the coordinator's history so every investigative step remains auditable.
Rely on subagent context isolation, requiring the subagent's final report to include the evidence the coordinator needs.

questions.question: You are designing how the "lookup_order" tool reports its outcomes so the agent can respond correctly when the order backend times out or when a search simply finds no matching orders. Which TWO behaviors are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Return a result with "is_error" set to true and a descriptive failure message when the backend lookup times out.
Report both timeouts and zero-match lookups through one generic "lookup unavailable" status to keep agent handling simple.
Return a successful result containing an empty match list when the query completes but no orders match the criteria.
Return an empty result marked as success when the backend times out, so the agent proceeds as if no orders exist.

questions.question: Human agents who receive escalations cannot view the agent's conversation. They report that escalated tickets arrive with only a brief issue label, forcing them to re-investigate every case from scratch. What change best fixes this?

options.text: Require the escalate_to_human input schema to capture customer ID, root cause findings, order and amount details, and a recommended action.
Include a customer sentiment summary and an urgency rating with each escalation so humans can prioritize incoming cases correctly.
Attach the complete raw tool outputs from the session to each ticket so the human has every piece of evidence gathered.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the agent to always write thorough, detailed notes whenever it escalates a case to a human.

questions.question: To guarantee identity verification, the team wants Claude's first turn to always call "get_customer" instead of answering in text or selecting a different tool. On a model that supports forced tool use, which "tool_choice" configuration achieves this?

options.text: Set "tool_choice" to type "tool" with name "get_customer" on the first request.
Set "strict" to true on the "get_customer" tool definition to enforce its invocation.
Keep "tool_choice" as "auto" and add a system prompt rule that "get_customer" always runs first.
Set "tool_choice" to "any" so the model is required to call one of the available tools.

questions.question: The agent outputs a confidence score with each automated resolution, and overall accuracy measures 96%. Leadership wants to stop human review of high-confidence cases. Which TWO practices should be in place before making this change? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Break accuracy down by request type and extracted field instead of trusting the aggregate figure.
Have the agent re-rate its own confidence after drafting each resolution and route on that rating.
Audit a stratified random sample of high-confidence resolutions regularly to detect new error patterns.
Raise the confidence threshold for automation and accept the aggregate accuracy as sufficient evidence.

questions.question: The coordinator retrieves customer and order records with "get_customer" and "lookup_order", then spawns a billing subagent whose Task prompt says only "Analyze the duplicate charge claim." The subagent replies that it has no customer or order data. What change resolves this?

options.text: Include the retrieved customer and order details directly in the subagent's Task prompt.
Retry the delegation, since subagent context loading can fail transiently on first invocation.
Add a system prompt instruction directing the subagent to consult the coordinator's conversation history.
Increase the subagent's context window allocation so the parent's full history can fit inside it.

questions.question: The agent decomposes a request involving a billing dispute and a separate return into two independent investigations delegated to subagents. Which two implementation choices correctly run both subagents in parallel and return their results? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set "disable_parallel_tool_use" to true within "tool_choice" so each Task invocation runs independently.
Return all subagent results as tool result blocks in one message on the next request.
Have the coordinator emit both Task tool calls within a single assistant response.
Feed each subagent's result back to the coordinator in its own separate message as it completes.

questions.question: The team's "lookup_order" tool currently returns "isError": true with the message "No matching orders found" whenever a customer genuinely has no orders on file. The agent responds by retrying the lookup repeatedly and then escalating to a human. What change to the tool's response design fixes this?
