options.text: Keep "isError" set to true but expand the message to state that no orders exist and retrying will not help.
Add a system prompt rule instructing the agent to treat no-match error messages as final answers.
Return a successful result containing an empty order list, reserving error responses for actual failures.
Have the agent retry the lookup with broader search parameters whenever no matches come back.

questions.question: A developer implements the company's $300 autonomous refund cap as a PostToolUse hook with the matcher "mcp__billing__process_refund". Production logs show over-cap refunds still complete because the hook fires only after the tool has executed. What change enforces the cap?

options.text: Replace it with a PreToolUse hook that inspects the "tool_input" amount and returns a "deny" decision for over-cap refunds.
Convert the enforcement logic to an async hook so it evaluates the refund without delaying the agent loop.
Add the $300 cap to the refund tool's description so the model sees the limit when constructing each call.
Keep the PostToolUse hook but have it return an error result so Claude issues a compensating reversal for over-cap refunds.

questions.question: While resolving a billing dispute, the agent requests "get_customer" and "lookup_order" in a single assistant turn. The "get_customer" call succeeds, but "lookup_order" times out against the backend. How should your code send the tool results back to Claude?

options.text: Send the "get_customer" result now, then send a second user message with the "lookup_order" outcome after a retry.
Return only the successful "get_customer" result, so Claude can re-issue the "lookup_order" request on its next turn.
Return one "tool_result" block for each requested call, marking the "lookup_order" result with "is_error" set to true.
Return the "get_customer" result plus a plain text sentence explaining that the order lookup timed out.

questions.question: The team is formalizing the JSON handoff that the "escalate_to_human" tool delivers to the human ticket queue. Which two practices should the team apply when designing this structured handoff? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate each handoff against a JSON schema requiring fields like customer ID, root cause, refund amount, and recommended action.
Have the agent self-rate its confidence in each summary and suppress any handoff that scores below a defined threshold.
Put customer IDs and refund amounts in field values, not in schema field names or enum values.
Attach the full raw conversation transcript and every tool result so the receiving human can reconstruct the case independently.

questions.question: Production traces show the agent often calls "escalate_to_human" for routine refunds and calls "process_refund" for disputes that need human approval. Both tools currently carry one-sentence descriptions. Which TWO changes most directly improve tool selection? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set "tool_choice" to "any" so the model is guaranteed to call a tool on every request.
Expand each description with the inputs it expects, what it returns, and its policy constraints.
Add a retry step that re-invokes the model with stronger wording whenever the wrong tool is called.
Rewrite both descriptions to state when each tool applies and when the other should be used instead.

questions.question: A developer is adding a billing-investigation subagent with an AgentDefinition. Policy requires that this subagent can read customer and order data but must never be able to call "process_refund". Which configuration guarantees this restriction?

options.text: Write the "description" field to say the agent only investigates, so refund work is never delegated to it.
Set the definition's "tools" field to only "get_customer" and "lookup_order", omitting "process_refund".
Omit the "tools" field and state in the subagent's system prompt that it must never issue refunds.
Rely on the subagent automatically inheriting only the tools the coordinator actually used in the current turn.

questions.question: The team wants a shared GitHub MCP server available to every engineer who clones the repository, while one engineer privately tests an experimental log-parsing server. Which TWO configuration choices are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Commit the experimental log-parsing server to ".mcp.json" so teammates can evaluate it before it is finalized.
Add the shared GitHub server to each engineer's "~/.claude.json" so no MCP configuration file needs to be committed.
Register the experimental log-parsing server with user scope so it is stored in "~/.claude.json" and stays private.
Define the shared GitHub server in ".mcp.json" at the project root and commit that file to version control.

questions.question: After the team added the line "always search for relevant context before answering" to the system prompt, logs show the agent calling the MCP tool "search_wiki" even for code-content lookups where Grep is appropriate. Both tools already have clear, distinct descriptions. What change most directly fixes the misrouting?

options.text: Force Grep with "tool_choice" as the first call on every request so code lookups always run first.
Add a routing classifier that inspects each request and selects Grep or the wiki tool before delegation.
Reword the instruction to describe the goal, removing the word "search", which matches the wiki tool's name.
Expand both tool descriptions with boundary language distinguishing code lookups from wiki content searches.

questions.question: Engineers ask the agent to add comprehensive tests to an undocumented legacy module. Coverage gaps, dependencies, and needed mocks are all unknown until the agent explores the code. Which task decomposition approach fits this work?

options.text: Use dynamic decomposition: map the module structure first, then generate subtasks from what each pass discovers.
Provide the entire module in one large prompt so the agent can plan all tests in a single pass.
Define a fixed prompt chain up front, running the same predetermined sequence of passes for every module.
Have the agent self-rate confidence after writing each test and retry any step rated below a threshold.

questions.question: The agent's system prompt instructs it to read the team's conventions file before generating any boilerplate files. Logs show that in 8% of runs it calls Write without reading the conventions first, producing code that breaks the conventions. What change guarantees the required ordering?

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt showing the conventions file being read before every Write.
Restate the ordering rule at the top of the system prompt in capitalized, emphatic wording.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks Write calls until the conventions file has been read in the session.
Add a PostToolUse hook on Write that detects when the conventions file was  and alerts Claude.

questions.question: Engineers operating this system want an audit trail recording every subagent the main agent spawns and when each one completes, captured reliably even on unattended runs. Which implementation provides this?

options.text: Have each subagent write its own completion entry to a shared log file as its final step.
Instruct the agent in its system prompt to announce every subagent it spawns and summarize each completion.
Parse the agent's final response text for mentions of subagent activity and store any matches.
Register "SubagentStart" and "SubagentStop" hooks that log each delegation and completion as they fire.

questions.question: While tracing empty-interface usage through a legacy Go service, the agent calls Grep with the pattern "interface{}", and the call fails with a regex diagnostic error. What should the agent do to complete the search?

options.text: Escape the curly braces in the pattern, since Grep interprets patterns as regular expressions.
Set "multiline" to true so a pattern containing braces can match across line boundaries.
Switch to Glob for the search, since brace characters belong to file path matching syntax.
Add retry logic around the call, since rejected patterns are usually transient tool errors.

questions.question: To make the agent use another tool instead of Grep for symbol searches across repositories, the team added a system prompt rule: always use the MCP "code_search" tool instead of Grep. The agent now calls "code_search" even for simple single-file string lookups, producing slow results full of irrelevant matches. What is the best fix?

options.text: Add harness logic that reruns any poor "code_search" result through Grep automatically before returning it to the agent.
Introduce a routing tool the agent must call first, which returns the name of the correct search tool for each query.
Keep the system prompt rule and add a permission deny rule that removes Grep from the agent's toolset entirely.
Replace the always-apply rule with boundary language in the "code_search" description stating when each search tool applies.

questions.question: Despite detailed, distinct tool descriptions, your agent calls a search tool on purely conversational questions and routes code searches between two tools inconsistently. Reviewing the system prompt, you find it states "Always call a tool first before responding" and contains two sections that each name a different tool as the mandatory choice for code searches. Which TWO findings should your review flag? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Flag the absence of few-shot examples demonstrating which tool should handle each request type.
Flag the instruction "Always call a tool first before responding" that applies to every request.
Flag the two sections that each name a different tool as the mandatory choice for code search tasks.
Flag that the system prompt comes after the tool definitions in the final prompt.

questions.question: While automating a repetitive migration task, an agent discovers an undocumented external API dependency mid-run and adds a mocking subtask that was never part of its original plan. Which loop design makes this adaptive behavior possible?

options.text: Enable extended thinking so the model anticipates all contingencies, including hidden dependencies, before execution begins.
Feed each tool result back into the model so it chooses the next action based on what was discovered.
Run the loop with no turn limit so the agent keeps iterating until every subtask completes.
Enumerate every possible subtask during initial planning and activate whichever ones match conditions at runtime.

questions.question: The coordinator delegates codebase survey subtasks to parallel subagents, but completed surveys repeatedly omit entire subsystems even though every subagent finishes its assignment successfully. Which two changes most effectively address this coverage problem? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Move the subagents to a model with a larger context window so each one can analyze more files per task.
Instruct each subagent to broaden its investigation beyond its assigned area whenever it encounters related code paths.
Have the coordinator review the aggregated findings for coverage gaps and delegate follow-up subtasks to fill them.
Have the coordinator give each subagent an explicit objective and boundaries so the subtasks together span the codebase.

questions.question: While the agent is exploring a legacy codebase, a Bash tool call it requested fails with a permission error. How should your loop report this failure before the next request to Claude?

options.text: Retry the identical Bash call automatically until it succeeds before sending anything back to Claude.
Return a "tool_result" block with "is_error" set to true containing the error message, then continue the loop.
End the loop and show the raw error to the engineer, since the agent cannot continue without that output.
Append the error text as a new assistant message so Claude sees the failure in its own conversation turn.

questions.question: A coordinator delegates codebase discovery to one subagent and boilerplate generation to another. A teammate suggests the discovery subagent hand its findings directly to the generation subagent to reduce latency. What is the best design decision?

options.text: Adopt the direct hand-off, since both subagents already share the coordinator's conversation history and findings.
Route through the coordinator so it observes all interactions, handles errors uniformly, and controls what each subagent receives.
Adopt the direct hand-off but require each subagent to attach a self-rated confidence score so the coordinator can audit afterward.
Adopt the direct hand-off and rely on retry logic inside each subagent to recover from any failures along the path.

questions.question: The team adds a rule file at ".claude/rules/testing.md" with a "paths" field of test-file glob patterns. During a session spent entirely generating boilerplate in "src/handlers/", the testing conventions never appear in the loaded context. Why is this the expected behavior?

options.text: Rules with a "paths" field are evaluated once at launch and  when no matching file exists yet.
The rule file must be referenced from the project CLAUDE.md with an "@import" line before it can load.
Glob patterns in "paths" must name directories, so file-extension patterns never match anything.
Path-scoped rules load only when a file matching the glob is read, written, or edited.

questions.question: An engineer asks the agent to add a caching layer to a legacy billing service, an unfamiliar domain where invalidation strategy and failure modes have not yet been considered. Which technique best brings out these design questions before implementation begins?

options.text: Run the task in plan mode so Claude explores the codebase read-only and proposes an implementation plan for review.
Have Claude interview the engineer with clarifying questions about edge cases, concerns, and tradeoffs first.
Write a detailed upfront specification covering every requirement, then have Claude implement it directly.
Provide two or three concrete input and output examples so Claude infers the expected behavior unambiguously.

questions.question: This team defines a codebase-exploration subagent whose AgentDefinition omits the "tools" field. Logs show the subagent sometimes editing files and running build commands while answering questions about legacy modules. What change most reliably confines it to read-only exploration?

options.text: State in the subagent's system prompt that it must never write files or execute shell commands.
Attach a hook that records every Write and Bash invocation to an audit log for review.
Add Read, Grep, and Glob to the parent options' "allowedTools" so those tools are auto-approved.
Set the subagent's "tools" field to list only Read, Grep, and Glob.

questions.question: The team's review chain for legacy modules runs a per-file analysis stage, then a cross-file integration pass. The per-file stage returns verbose free-form prose, so the integration pass receives oversized, hard-to-parse input and misses cross-file issues. What should they change?

options.text: Merge both stages into a single prompt that performs per-file analysis and integration together.
Have the per-file stage return structured findings constrained by a JSON schema instead of prose.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the per-file stage to keep each file's findings brief.
Switch the cross-file integration pass to a model variant offering a larger context window.

questions.question: After Claude drafts a new API endpoint, your review finds two fixes that depend on each other (the validation logic and the error response format) plus one unrelated variable naming issue. How should you deliver this feedback?

options.text: Clear the session and restart with a stronger prompt that restates every requirement up front.
Describe the two interacting fixes together in one message, then fix the naming issue in a follow-up.
Send each of the three fixes one at a time, letting Claude fully complete each before starting the next.
Spawn a parallel subagent for each of the three issues so all the fixes land at the same time.

questions.question: A team lead added permission rules that auto-approve the project's test runner to their own "~/.claude/settings.json", but every teammate is still prompted before tests run. Which two actions correctly resolve this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reserve "~/.claude/settings.json" for personal preferences, since it applies only to that user across projects.
Have teammates pull the repository so they receive the team lead's user-level settings file automatically.
Move the shared permission rules into ".claude/settings.json" and commit the file to the repository.
Add the approval rules to the project root CLAUDE.md so every teammate's sessions enforce them.

questions.question: A developer split a long project CLAUDE.md into topic files pulled in with "@path" imports, expecting to save context, but every session still loads all of the content. Which change reduces the context loaded in a typical session?

options.text: Move the topic files into ".claude/rules/" and add "paths" globs so each loads only for matching files.
Merge related topics back together so the CLAUDE.md uses fewer "@path" import references overall.
Run /compact at the start of every session so the imported rule content gets summarized early.
Move the imported topic files into each developer's user-level CLAUDE.md in their home directory.

questions.question: Your team is triaging a backlog and deciding how plan mode should be applied before Claude Code writes any code. Which two approaches follow the documented guidance? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use plan mode for work in an unfamiliar part of the codebase that needs exploration before any edits.
Use plan mode for a change that touches dozens of files and has several viable implementation approaches.
Use plan mode for a single-file bug fix that has a clear stack trace and an obvious correction.
Use plan mode when a task must finish quickly, since it skips exploratory file reads to save tokens.

questions.question: A teammate proposes a team policy: every change goes through plan mode first, including one-line fixes like correcting a typo in an error message, arguing that reviewing a plan always lowers risk. What should you advise?

options.text: Handle small, clear fixes with direct execution and reserve plan mode for changes with uncertain scope or approach.
Keep the policy but instruct Claude to write shorter plans for small fixes so review takes less time.
Adopt the policy, since reviewing a plan before any execution reduces risk regardless of change size.
Use direct execution for every change and rely on version control to revert any complex change that goes wrong later.

questions.question: You give Claude Code a failing test suite for a new parsing utility and let it iterate until every test passes. Reviewing the diff, you find the function returns hardcoded values chosen to match each test's exact inputs. What prompt change prevents this?

options.text: Configure automatic retries that rerun the generation until the full suite passes on two consecutive attempts.
Switch to plan mode so Claude proposes an implementation design for review before writing any production code.
Instruct Claude to write a general-purpose solution for all valid inputs, treating the tests as verification only.
Have Claude rate its own confidence that the implementation generalizes and accept only high-confidence runs.

questions.question: Claude Code generates structured release-note entries from merged pull requests, and a human currently reviews every entry. Aggregate accuracy measures 97%, and the team wants to cut review effort. Which TWO steps should come first? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Treat passing JSON schema validation as sufficient evidence of accuracy, since valid structured output confirms correctness.
Break accuracy down by pull request type and by output field to confirm performance is stable across segments.
Have the model self-rate its confidence per entry and automate everything scored above a fixed threshold.
Audit a stratified random sample of high-confidence entries to detect error patterns the aggregate metric hides.

questions.question: Your team runs a scripted multi-hour refactoring job that coordinates several agent phases across the codebase. When the process crashes partway through, restarts redo work that earlier phases already completed. Which design enables reliable crash recovery?

options.text: Resume the crashed session with "--resume" so the conversation transcript shows the agent which files were already handled.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction directing the agent to always continue from where the previous run stopped.
Have each phase export its progress to structured state files, and load a manifest on restart to identify remaining work.
Restart the migration from the first file each time, relying on the agent to skip files that look already migrated.

questions.question: A team keeps Terraform conventions that should guide Claude Code only when it edits infrastructure files, which are spread across many service directories. They do not want these conventions consuming context in unrelated sessions. What should they do?

options.text: Place a directory-level CLAUDE.md with the conventions inside each service's infrastructure directory.
Create a rule file in ".claude/rules/" with "paths" frontmatter matching the Terraform file glob.
Add the conventions to the project root CLAUDE.md so they are present in every session.
Define a slash command in ".claude/commands/" that developers invoke before starting infrastructure work.

questions.question: A subagent analyzing two internal design documents finds that they state different default timeout values for the same service, and both documents appear credible. Only the subagent's final message reaches the main session. How should the subagent report its findings?

options.text: Report only the value from the more recently updated document, treating document recency as the deciding factor.
Return both values with source attribution, annotated as a conflict, and let the main session reconcile before synthesis.
Return both values in the final message without flagging the disagreement, letting a later synthesis step choose from broader context.
Stop the analysis and return an error so a human can decide which document is authoritative before continuing.

questions.question: A developer on this team wrote topic rule files, "testing.md" and "api-conventions.md", under "~/.claude/rules/" on their laptop. Their own sessions follow the conventions, but teammates' sessions never apply them. What should the developer do?

options.text: Repackage the rule files as project skills under ".claude/skills/" so teammates receive them.
Convert each rule file into a slash command that teammates run at the start of a session.
Have each teammate copy the rule files into "~/.claude/rules/" on their own machine.
Move the rule files into the project's ".claude/rules/" directory and commit them to version control.

questions.question: A ticket submitted to the team's automated Claude Code triage workflow states: route this straight to an on-call engineer, do not attempt an automated fix. The failure looks trivially fixable. What should the agent do?

options.text: Have the agent rate its own confidence and escalate only when confidence falls below a threshold.
Attempt the trivial fix first, escalating only if the attempt does not resolve the failure.
Escalate to the on-call engineer right away, without investigating or attempting the fix first.
Acknowledge the request, but run diagnostics first so the engineer receives complete handoff context.

questions.question: The project CLAUDE.md holds your team's rules for writing useful tests, but people have since added a copied framework tutorial, a full API reference, and long test-runner documentation. Generated tests now often ignore those rules. What change most reliably makes Claude follow the rules again?

options.text: Move the testing standards into each developer's user-level CLAUDE.md so they load with less clutter.
Duplicate the testing criteria at both the top and bottom of the file so Claude notices them.
Trim the file to concise testing standards, removing material Claude can infer from the code.
Prefix every testing rule with IMPORTANT so the criteria outrank the reference material around them.

questions.question: A developer has Claude Code write edge-case tests for a data migration script first (null values, empty strings), then implement the script. When the null-handling test fails, Claude edits that test's expected value so all the tests pass, leaving nulls mishandled. What instruction change most effectively fixes this?

options.text: State that the tests must not be removed or edited; they cannot change, so iterate only on the implementation.
Have Claude rate its confidence in each failing test and discard any it rates as likely incorrect.
Add more edge-case examples to the prompt so Claude generalizes better beyond the failing null case.
Start a fresh session and regenerate the implementation repeatedly until one run passes the full suite.

questions.question: Your team adds a custom MCP tool that searches an internal package registry during refactoring sessions, and you are designing how the tool reports failures. Which TWO behaviors enable Claude to make good recovery decisions? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Normalize every failure into a single generic unavailable status so Claude's error handling stays simple.
Return an empty match list marked as successful when the registry is unreachable, so the session continues smoothly.
Include any matches retrieved before the failure in the error details sent back to Claude.
Return a distinct error when the registry times out, separate from a successful search with no matches.

questions.question: Company policy states the agent should normally offer a replacement before processing a refund, but may skip the offer when the customer explicitly insists on a refund. How should you implement this policy?

options.text: Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks every "process_refund" call until a replacement has been offered.
Route all refund requests through "escalate_to_human" so a person decides whether to offer a replacement first.
Add a PostToolUse hook on the refund tool that flags any refund issued without a prior replacement offer.
State the guideline in the system prompt, since applying it correctly requires per-case judgment.

questions.question: Billing disputes the agent handles vary widely: duplicate charges, missed discounts, overlapping subscriptions. The correct investigation steps only become clear after seeing the customer's account data. How should the agent plan its investigation?

options.text: Define a fixed checklist of tool calls that every dispute follows in the same order.
Classify each dispute first and route it to one of several predefined tool pipelines.
Raise the loop's maximum turn limit so the agent can work through longer checklists.
Have the agent map the account state first, then generate subtasks from what it discovers.

questions.question: After investigating a billing dispute, the main agent delegates drafting of the customer reply to a resolution-drafting subagent. The drafts repeatedly omit the dispute amounts and order IDs the main agent already retrieved. What change most effectively fixes this?

options.text: Increase the subagent's context allocation so more of the parent conversation carries over into its window.
Grant the drafting subagent the backend MCP tools so it can re-query the customer and order data itself.
Add a system prompt instruction directing the subagent to consult the main agent's conversation history.
Pass the complete investigation findings, including amounts and order IDs, in the drafting subagent's prompt.

questions.question: The team designs a coordinator agent that delegates billing-dispute investigation and order-history investigation to two separate subagents. Which two design decisions correctly reflect how this hub-and-spoke architecture works? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the two subagents exchange messages directly with each other to reconcile any overlapping findings before reporting their results.
Rely on each subagent automatically inheriting the coordinator's full conversation history so case details never need restating when delegating.
Handle subagent failures in the coordinator, which decides whether to retry the task, delegate it again, or proceed with partial results.
Keep each subagent's intermediate tool calls and results isolated in its own context and have it return only a final report to the coordinator.

questions.question: Company policy caps autonomous refunds at $200, and the team also wants the agent to generally attempt a resolution before escalating. Which two design choices correctly match each rule to the appropriate mechanism? (Select TWO.)

options.text: State the $200 cap in the system prompt with strong emphasis so the model is guaranteed never to exceed it.
Use a "PostToolUse" hook to reject process_refund calls above $200 so a refund over the limit never runs.
Enforce the refund cap with a "PreToolUse" hook that denies any process_refund call over $200 before it runs.
Put the preference to attempt resolution before escalating in the system prompt, knowing it is not always followed.

questions.question: The agent spends several tool calls each session discovering which refund policies, return windows, and order-status codes exist. Which TWO changes supply this reference data without requiring the agent to invoke any tool to obtain it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Expose the returns policy documents and refund eligibility rules as MCP resources the agent can read directly.
Expose the "process_refund" action as an MCP resource so the agent issues refunds by reading a resource URI.
Create a "get_reference_data" tool the agent must call first in every session to retrieve policy details.
Publish the backend order-status codes and customer record schema as a read-only MCP resource catalog.

questions.question: In production, some of the agent's final replies to customers end abruptly mid-sentence. The loop runs tools while "stop_reason" is "tool_use" and presents the response as finished whenever it is any other value. What should the team change?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the model to keep every customer reply concise enough to fit the output limit.
Detect truncation by checking whether the final text block ends with end punctuation, such as a period, and retry the request when it does not.
Branch on the exact stop reason, treating "end_turn" as complete and handling "max_tokens" as a truncated reply.
Lower the sampling temperature so the model produces shorter and more predictable responses.

questions.question: During testing, the harness returns the "lookup_order" output in a user message that places a brief explanatory text block before the "tool_result" block. The API rejects the request with a 400 formatting error. What should the developer change?

options.text: Move the "tool_result" into an assistant message so it directly follows the "tool_use" turn.
Retry the request with backoff, since transient formatting errors typically resolve on resubmission.
Set "is_error" to true on the "tool_result" so the API tolerates the nonstandard block order.
Reorder the user message so the "tool_result" block appears before any text content.

questions.question: A developer spent yesterday tracing an occasional double-billing defect in a Claude Code session they named billing-probe. Several unrelated sessions have since run in the same project directory. Which command lets them continue exactly that investigation today?

options.text: Run "claude --resume billing-probe" to restore the named session and its full conversation context.
Run "claude -p" with a prompt summarizing the prior investigation to continue it.
Start a new session and rely on CLAUDE.md to reload the investigation's discovered findings.
Run "claude --continue", which reloads the most recent conversation in the working directory.

questions.question: The team wants the agent to create Jira tickets whenever it escalates a case to a human. The refund workflow enforces company-specific policy rules. Which TWO integration decisions follow the recommended approach? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Replace the custom refund tools with a general-purpose MCP server that runs database queries directly.
Build a custom Jira MCP server so the team fully controls its tool descriptions.
Keep the refund and escalation logic in a custom MCP server built for this workflow.
Connect an existing Jira MCP server from the connector directory instead of building one.

questions.question: The "lookup_order" tool returns one message, "Error: request could not be processed", for timeouts, malformed order IDs, and missing orders alike. The agent retries unrecoverable failures and abandons transient ones. What change most directly fixes this?

options.text: Add a system prompt rule instructing the agent to retry every failed "lookup_order" call three times before escalating.
Return errors that name the failure cause and include an "errorCategory" and "isRetryable" flag the agent can read.
Have the agent rate its own confidence after each failure and escalate to a human whenever that confidence is low.
Catch failures inside the MCP server and return an empty result marked successful so the agent is never confused by errors.

questions.question: Yesterday an engineer paused a long Claude Code investigation into this agent's refund flow in a session named refund-triage. Overnight, a teammate modified two of the MCP tool handler files. The engineer runs "claude --resume refund-triage" today. What should the first prompt do?

options.text: Continue the investigation directly, since resuming restores prior tool results that reflect current file contents.
Run /compact first so stale tool outputs are removed by the summary and Claude fetches fresh versions.
Ask Claude to re-explore the entire tools directory so its understanding is rebuilt from current code.
Name the two modified files and instruct Claude to re-read them before continuing the analysis.

questions.question: Company policy requires that refunds above $500 be routed to "escalate_to_human" instead of executing. You are adding a "PreToolUse" hook to enforce this rule. Which hook design correctly blocks only the refund calls that break this rule?

options.text: Register the amount check as an asynchronous hook so policy evaluation runs without slowing down the agent loop.
Document the $500 limit in the "process_refund" tool description so the model declines to construct larger refund calls.
Match the hook on the "process_refund" tool name and inspect "tool_input" in the callback, denying calls where the amount exceeds $500.
Write a matcher expression that fires only when the "process_refund" call's "amount" argument is above $500, so compliant refunds skip the hook.

questions.question: A validation run shows the agent selects the correct resolution action in 97% of cases overall. Based on this figure, leadership wants to remove human review of refund approvals. What should the team verify first?

options.text: Add a self-check pass where the agent re-evaluates each decision before acting on it.
Have the agent rate its own confidence and automate only the cases it rates highly.
Break down accuracy by request category, such as billing disputes, before removing human review.
Expand the validation set with more sampled cases and confirm the 97% figure still holds overall.

questions.question: A customer opens with: "This is ridiculous, you charged me twice for order #4521 and I am furious." The issue is a routine duplicate charge the agent can correct. How should the agent respond?

options.text: Acknowledge the frustration, then offer the refund, escalating only if the customer explicitly asks for a human.
Have the agent self-rate its confidence and call "escalate_to_human" when the rating falls below a set cutoff.
Score the message with sentiment analysis and escalate whenever the detected frustration exceeds a defined threshold.
Call "escalate_to_human" right away, treating the customer's strong negative language as an explicit demand for human assistance.

questions.question: Some source documents report two different figures for the same financial metric, each tied to a distinct methodology. The current schema stores one value, so one figure is dropped without any warning. How should the team redesign the output?

options.text: Average the two figures into a single compromise value so the schema stays single-valued.
Have the model attach a confidence score to each value and output only the higher-rated figure.
Have the model select whichever figure it judges more credible and output only that value.
Output both values with their sources and stated methodologies, marked with a conflict flag.

questions.question: The extraction schema already captures "line_items", "stated_total", "calculated_total", and "conflict_detected". The downstream billing integration requires that "calculated_total" actually equal the sum of the line item amounts. Where should this consistency rule be enforced?

options.text: Enable strict tool use so the API checks extracted values against the schema during generation.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the model to verify its arithmetic carefully before producing output.
Express the equality as a numeric constraint in the JSON schema so conforming output is guaranteed correct.
Compute the sum in application code after parsing and retry with the specific validation error on mismatch.

questions.question: Each week, the team must extract data from a batch of documents from a 40,000-document archive, and the results are due to a downstream compliance system every Friday at 9 AM. They want the 50% discount from the Message Batches API. How should they schedule batch submissions to meet the deadline reliably?

options.text: Rely on batches typically completing within one hour and submit each one shortly before the deadline.
Move the archive processing to synchronous API calls so every document completes before the deadline.
Submit each batch at least 24 hours before the results deadline to cover the maximum processing window.
Split the archive into many small batches so each individual batch is guaranteed to finish faster.

questions.question: The extraction schema includes a per-value confidence score the model fills in. An audit finds several fabricated values that carried confidence scores above 0.9, so routing by the confidence field alone misses them. Which verification approach most effectively catches these fabrications?

options.text: Strengthen the extraction prompt to instruct the model to report only values it is completely certain appear in the document.
Add a verification pass that locates a supporting quote in the source document for each value and flags values without one.
Raise the downstream acceptance threshold so only values with self-reported confidence above 0.98 are passed to downstream systems.
Run each extraction twice with the same prompt and accept only values on which both runs agree.

questions.question: Mid-session, the main agent establishes normalization rules for date and currency fields, then spawns a subagent to extract data from a batch of edge-case documents. The subagent's structured output ignores those rules entirely. What change fixes this?

options.text: Pass the normalization rules explicitly in the delegation prompt sent to the subagent.
Move the normalization rules into the main agent's system prompt so subagents inherit them.
Instruct the subagent to consult the earlier conversation turns where the rules were defined.
Retry the subagent call until its output conforms to the established normalization rules.

questions.question: Reviewer capacity is limited, so only a subset of extractions can receive human review before results flow to downstream systems. Which TWO routing approaches best target review at the extractions most likely to contain errors? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use per-field confidence scores for routing only after tests on labeled data show they predict errors.
Route extractions from ambiguous or poorly structured source documents to human review.
Ask the model to rate its own overall confidence and auto-approve extractions rated above a fixed cutoff.
Analyze the emotional tone of each incoming document's language and route strongly negative documents to review.

questions.question: The first full batch run extracts data from 12,000 vendor contracts, but 9% of the results fail JSON schema and business-rule validation, with failures concentrated in contracts that use tabular layouts instead of narrative text. What is the most cost-effective way to resolve this?

options.text: Move the failed contracts to individual synchronous API calls processed one at a time with the same prompt.
Improve the prompt using a sample of the failing contracts, then resubmit only those requests, identified by "custom_id".
Resubmit the entire 12,000-contract batch with an added instruction telling the model to follow the schema more carefully.
Configure an automatic retry loop that re-runs each failed extraction with the same unchanged prompt up to three times.

questions.question: After each extraction, the same conversation that produced the output is asked to review it for values put in the wrong field. These reviews approve nearly every extraction, yet downstream schema and business-rule validation keeps finding values in the wrong fields. What change most effectively improves review quality?

options.text: Have a separate Claude instance review each extraction without access to the generating session's context.
Strengthen the same-session prompt with an explicit instruction to double-check every field before approving.
Switch the review to a model with a larger context window so it can re-read the full document.
Ask the model to report a confidence score for each field and accept only high-confidence reviews.

questions.question: To catch extraction errors before data reaches downstream systems, the team added a verification step: they resume the extraction session and ask Claude to check its own output. The verifier approves almost every extraction, including several later found to contain wrong values. What change would most improve error detection?

options.text: Have the extractor rate its own confidence per field and route only low-confidence extractions to verification.
Enable extended thinking for the verification turn so the model thinks more thoroughly before approving.
Add an instruction in the resumed session directing Claude to be skeptical of its earlier extraction.
Run verification in a separate Claude instance given only the source document and the extracted JSON.

questions.question: Part of the pipeline uses a client-executed "lookup_reference" tool that the application runs during the conversation to find the cited source documents. The team wants to cut costs with the Message Batches API. Which TWO statements accurately guide this migration? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep extractions that need the application to run the lookup tool during the conversation on the synchronous API.
Submit everything in one batch, then append "tool_result" blocks to it after the application runs the lookup tool.
Move documents that need no client tool calls to batch, matching results to inputs by "custom_id".
Set "tool_choice" to "any" in each batch request so the batch worker executes the lookup tool during processing.

questions.question: The pipeline's document-fetch tool returns the same generic "document unavailable" error whether a file is corrupted, the storage backend times out, or the document ID is invalid. The agent now retries unrecoverable failures and abandons transient ones. What change best enables correct recovery decisions?

options.text: Return an empty extraction result marked as success so downstream processing continues without interruption.
Instruct the agent in the system prompt to retry every unavailable document twice before skipping it.
Add automatic exponential backoff retries inside the tool for every failure before reporting unavailability.
Return structured errors that include the failure category and whether the failure is retryable.

questions.question: The team's extraction prompt tells Claude to "flag any document with low data quality" so flagged documents go to human review. Reviewers report inconsistent routing: clean invoices get flagged while clearly unreadable documents are not flagged. What change most improves routing consistency?

options.text: Reword the instruction to stress that only genuinely problematic documents should be flagged for review.
Define concrete flag conditions, such as totals that do not add up or missing required identifier fields.
Run the extraction twice on each document and flag only documents both runs mark as low quality.
Have the model output a confidence score for each document and route those below a threshold.

questions.question: A team replaces its plain-text "respond with JSON" prompt with an extraction tool whose "input_schema" is the target JSON schema, setting "strict" to true on the tool definition and parsing results from the tool call. Which TWO statements accurately describe the reliability this change provides? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Stronger prompt wording alone would deliver the same syntax guarantees without defining a tool.
Semantic checks, such as verifying line items sum to the stated total, still need code-side validation.
Syntax-level failures such as malformed JSON and missing required fields are eliminated.
Schema conformance also ensures each extracted value is placed in the semantically correct field.

questions.question: The team wants each response to contain a brief text note describing document ambiguities before the extraction tool call, but with "tool_choice" set to the "any" type the note never appears despite clear prompt instructions. What change resolves this?

options.text: Switch "tool_choice" to the "auto" type and instruct Claude in the prompt to call the extraction tool after writing the note.
Set "strict" to true on the extraction tool so responses include both explanatory text and schema-valid tool input.
Raise "max_tokens" so the response has room for both the ambiguity note and the structured extraction call.
Keep the "any" tool choice and add a stronger system prompt section demanding the note be written before the tool invocation.

questions.question: The system's validation step confirms extracted vendor IDs through a "lookup_reference" tool. The tool returns an empty list both when the reference service times out and when no matching record exists, so outages get logged as missing vendors. How should the tool's responses be redesigned?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling Claude to treat empty lookup results as potential service failures.
Have the tool mark timed-out lookups as successful empty results so downstream processing continues uninterrupted.
Have the tool set "is_error" to true on timeouts, keeping no-match lookups as successful empty results.

questions.question: Logs show the coordinator spends its first several turns calling exploratory tools just to learn which document collections exist and how each is structured before it can delegate work. Which MCP capability best reduces this discovery overhead?

options.text: Raise the coordinator's tool-call budget so the exploratory phase can finish before delegation starts.
Add a custom discovery tool that returns the full data inventory when called at the start of each run.
Paste the current inventory of collections and their structures into the coordinator's system prompt.
Expose the collection catalog and structure summaries as MCP resources the coordinator reads directly.

questions.question: The coordinator's system prompt contains strict citation formatting rules, yet the report-generation subagent consistently produces reports that ignore them. Each subagent is defined programmatically with an AgentDefinition. What should you change?

options.text: Restate the citation rules at the top of the coordinator's system prompt with stronger emphasis.
Add a retry loop that regenerates the report whenever the citation format check fails.
Add the citation rules to the subagent's description field so Claude applies them during delegation.
Move the citation formatting rules into the report subagent's own system prompt in its AgentDefinition.

questions.question: Final reports frequently attach citations to the wrong sources. Logs show the search subagent returns its findings as free-form prose with URLs mentioned inline, which the synthesis agent's summaries then drop or mix up. What change most reliably preserves attribution?

options.text: Pass the full raw search output unmodified into the synthesis prompt so no source details are lost during aggregation.
Have the report generator re-run targeted web searches to locate a supporting source for each claim before adding citations.
Add a prose instruction to the synthesis agent's system prompt telling it to carefully preserve source references during summarization.
Require each subagent to return structured output pairing every claim with its source URL, document name, and publication date.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent uses Grep to search the document collection for a key statistic, but the tool returns only file paths. The agent needs the exact matching lines so it can quote them in the report. What is the most efficient approach?

options.text: Set "output_mode" to "count" to retrieve the number of matches found in each file.
Enable "multiline" so the search output includes the lines surrounding each match.
Set "output_mode" to "content" so the search returns matching lines with line numbers.
Use Read to load each file from the returned list and scan the full text for the matches.

questions.question: Reports cite sources correctly when the coordinator passes full subagent findings to the synthesis subagent. On long tasks, the coordinator first shortens the collected findings into a written summary to fit its context budget, and those reports leave out sources or link claims to the wrong source. What change most effectively restores correct attribution?

options.text: Require subagents to output structured claim-source mappings and keep them in the written summary.
Move the written summary to the beginning of the synthesis prompt to reduce the lost-in-the-middle effect.
Switch to a model with a larger context window so full findings reach synthesis without being shortened.
Strengthen the synthesis agent's system prompt with an explicit instruction to cite a source for every claim.

questions.question: The team is replacing the document analysis subagent's generic "fetch_url" tool with a constrained "load_document" tool after logs showed the subagent loading search results pages and forum threads. Which TWO design choices make the document-only restriction enforced by the system, not just suggested to the model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the tool implementation reject requests for sources outside the approved document repositories with a validation error.
Constrain the tool's "input_schema" so the parameter accepts a reference from the indexed document catalog rather than any URL string.
Add a system prompt rule stating that "load_document" must only be used for document retrieval, never for general web pages.
Set "strict" to true on the tool definition so grammar-constrained sampling guarantees only approved document sources are passed.

questions.question: Production traces show that requests to analyze uploaded PDFs often go to the search subagent's "process_content" tool. Its description ("processes content and returns key information") is almost the same as the description of the document subagent's "process_document" tool. Which change most directly resolves this misrouting?

options.text: Add a pre-delegation classifier that labels each incoming request as web research or document analysis.
Use a forced "tool_choice" setting to require the document tool whenever a request mentions a file.
Rename the search tool to "process_web_results" and limit its description to web search output.
Add few-shot routing examples to the coordinator's system prompt covering document versus web requests.

questions.question: Partway through a research run, the coordinator must escalate an unresolved conflict between two credible sources to a human analyst who has no access to any agent conversations. What should the escalation message contain?

options.text: An urgency rating plus timing data on how long each subagent ran, so the analyst can prioritize the case appropriately.
The complete raw outputs from every subagent so the analyst can work directly from all of the gathered evidence themselves.
A structured summary with the findings gathered so far and their sources, what is blocking progress, and a recommended next step.
Only the research topic and a conflict category label, so the analyst forms an independent judgment without anchoring bias.

questions.question: The web-search subagent's "search_scholar" tool returns the bare string "Error" for every failure. Logs show the agent retrying calls that were denied for lack of permission and abandoning simple timeouts. Which TWO changes to the tool's error response fix this recovery behavior? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a system prompt rule telling the agent to retry every failed tool call twice before moving on.
Add an "isRetryable" boolean alongside a human-readable description of what actually went wrong.
Include an "errorCategory" field distinguishing transient, validation, and permission failures.
Return failures as successful results with empty content so the workflow is not interrupted.

questions.question: Your document analysis subagent already returns JSON, but its schema requires a field containing the model's full step-by-step analysis for every claim, so each handoff still fills most of the synthesis agent's context budget. What change best resolves this?

options.text: Have the coordinator truncate each subagent's analysis field to a fixed length before forwarding it to synthesis.
Increase the synthesis agent's "max_tokens" setting so the larger structured handoffs fit within its request.
Replace the step-by-step analysis field with concise fields for key facts, evidence excerpts, and relevance scores.
Add a prompt instruction telling the subagent to keep its analysis field brief and tightly focused.

questions.question: While prototyping the search subagent's tool loop with the Messages API, a developer runs the requested search, then calls the API again with only the original user message plus a new user message containing the "tool_result" block. The request fails with a formatting error. What is the fix?

options.text: Add an explicit "is_error" field set to false so the API accepts the "tool_result" block.
Place the "tool_result" block inside an assistant message rather than a user message in the history.
Append the assistant message containing the "tool_use" block before the user message with the "tool_result".
Move the search output into the "system" field so it loads ahead of the conversation.

questions.question: While revising a drafted report, a subagent needs to change a deprecated citation label in only one place, but the label sits inside a boilerplate block that repeats identically 12 times, so Edit cannot obtain a unique match even with added surrounding context. What should the subagent do?

options.text: Use Read to load the entire file, then Write the complete updated content back.
Set "replace_all" to true so one Edit call rewrites the label in all 12 boilerplate blocks.
Extend "old_string" with more surrounding lines until the match becomes unique.
Switch to Bash and modify the targeted occurrence with a sed command.

questions.question: The document analysis subagent's generic "analyze_document" tool returns summaries, extracted figures, and verification results mixed together, and downstream agents read the output wrongly. The team is splitting it into "extract_data_points", "summarize_content", and "verify_claim_against_source". Which TWO design practices make the split effective? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Define a separate output format for each tool, returning only the fields that task produces.
Add a system prompt rule telling the subagent to retry whenever the returned result type looks wrong.
Reuse the original "analyze_document" description across all three tools so the model sees them as related.
Give each tool a description with boundary language stating when a sibling tool applies instead.

questions.question: While testing the document analysis subagent's loop, a response arrives whose "stop_reason" is "max_tokens" rather than "tool_use" or "end_turn". How should the loop handle this response?

options.text: Scan the response text for tool names and execute them, continuing the loop as if tools were requested.
Resend the identical request unchanged, repeating until the model eventually returns "end_turn".
Treat the response as truncated and retry the request with a higher output token limit before using it.
Treat it the same as "end_turn" and return the response to the coordinator as the completed result.

questions.question: Requests that mention uploaded reports frequently trigger the web-search subagent's "gather_info" tool instead of the document agent's "extract_info" tool; the two tools carry nearly identical one-line descriptions. Which TWO changes most directly fix the misrouting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Rewrite both tool descriptions with boundary language stating when each applies, such as uploaded files versus live web pages.
Set "tool_choice" to "any" in the coordinator's requests so Claude is guaranteed to call some tool instead of answering in text.
Rename the tools so each name signals its distinct function, for example "extract_web_results" for the web-search tool.
Enable strict tool use on both tool definitions so Claude's inputs always validate exactly against each input schema.

questions.question: For open-ended research topics, the coordinator always runs the same fixed sequence: search, analyze, synthesize, report. Subtopics found during analysis are never investigated, leaving coverage gaps in the final reports. What change addresses this?

options.text: Strengthen the synthesis subagent's prompt so it infers and fills missing subtopics from the findings it receives.
Increase each subagent's context window allocation so more sources fit within the existing fixed pipeline stages.
Switch to dynamic decomposition where the coordinator spawns new subtasks based on intermediate findings.
Add a fifth fixed step to the pipeline that reruns the web search subagent after document analysis completes.

questions.question: The pipeline's review prompt describes the required comment format (file, line, severity, suggested fix) in detailed prose, yet comments still vary in structure and severity labeling across runs despite several rewrites. What change most effectively produces consistent output?

options.text: Add two or three concrete examples pairing a sample finding with the exact expected comment.
Add a pipeline step that re-runs the review whenever the comment format differs from the last run.
Rewrite the formatting rules again, marking every required field as IMPORTANT.
Have Claude rate its confidence in each comment and discard comments below a threshold.

questions.question: A new pipeline step invokes Claude Code to review each pull request diff, but every run hangs until the runner's timeout kills the job because Claude Code launches its interactive session. What change fixes this?

options.text: Pipe an empty line to stdin so the interactive session receives input and terminates cleanly.
Invoke Claude Code with the "-p" flag so it prints the result and exits without waiting for input.
Add "--output-format json" so the run emits machine-readable output and terminates when it finishes.
Raise the CI job timeout so the interactive session has enough time to complete the review.

questions.question: You are defining the JSON schema that the review pipeline uses to extract findings from pull requests. Fields like the file path and severity are always determinable from the diff, but a referenced CVE identifier frequently is not. How should the schema handle these fields?

options.text: Keep all fields required and rely on a validation retry loop with error feedback to correct fabricated CVE identifiers.
Mark every field in the schema nullable so the model is never forced to supply a value it cannot verify.
Keep all fields required and instruct Claude in the prompt to output the string "unknown" when a value is missing.
Keep the always-present fields required and make only the CVE identifier nullable, allowing a JSON null value when absent.

questions.question: The pipeline's prompt instructs Claude to "handle null values gracefully" when generating tests for migration scripts. Across runs, the generated tests inconsistently expect nulls to be , defaulted, or rejected. What prompt change most effectively fixes this?

options.text: Have Claude rate its confidence in each generated test and discard low-confidence ones.
Rewrite the prose instruction with stronger wording stating null handling must be consistent.
Provide two or three concrete test cases showing a null input and its expected output.
Re-run test generation several times and keep only the tests that agree across runs.

questions.question: The code review system uses an extraction tool whose "input_schema" marks "cwe_id" as a required string in every finding. For non-security findings, Claude fills the field with plausible but invented identifiers. Which schema change best eliminates these fabricated values?

options.text: Add a validation-retry loop that returns fabricated identifiers to Claude with an error message.
Enable "strict: true" on the tool definition so inputs always conform exactly to the schema.
Add a system prompt rule telling Claude never to invent an identifier for non-security findings.
Make "cwe_id" nullable so Claude can return null when no identifier applies.

questions.question: The engineer who configured the automated reviews stored the team's review criteria in their own "~/.claude/CLAUDE.md". Reviews on their laptop follow the criteria, but pipeline runs ignore them and produce unfocused feedback. What should the engineer do?

options.text: Add the review criteria to the committed ".claude/settings.json" so the pipeline applies them.
Run /memory at the start of each CI job so the engineer's memory files are loaded.
Rewrite the CI prompt to tell Claude to review more conservatively and stay focused.
Move the review criteria into the project root CLAUDE.md and commit it to the repository.

questions.question: Before adding a complex new test-generation stage to the pipeline, the team had Claude interview them about edge cases, concerns, and tradeoffs, and the interview is now complete. According to Anthropic's recommended Claude Code workflow, what should happen next?

options.text: Continue implementing in the same session, since the interview answers are already loaded into context.
Run /compact to summarize the interview transcript, then implement within the compacted session.
Repeat the interview in plan mode so the answers become a plan the team can formally approve.
Have Claude write the full spec to a "SPEC.md" file, then implement it in a fresh session.

questions.question: The root CLAUDE.md contains 150 lines of test-generation conventions. Test files are spread across the repository, next to the code they test. Reviews of pull requests that change no test files still load those lines. What restructuring fixes this?

options.text: Place a directory-level CLAUDE.md containing the conventions inside every folder that holds test files.
Keep the conventions in CLAUDE.md but import them with "@standards/test-conventions.md" from a separate file.
Move the conventions into a ".claude/rules/" file with "paths" frontmatter globs matching the test files.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction telling Claude to apply the test conventions only when a pull request changes tests.

questions.question: The CI review step runs "claude -p" with "--output-format json" and "--json-schema". Sometimes, the script that posts inline PR comments crashes because the parsed response contains no "structured_output" field. How should the posting script handle responses robustly?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction stating that the structured findings must always be populated in every response.
Treat a run as valid only when the subtype is "success" and "structured_output" is present, failing otherwise.
Fall back to parsing the review findings out of the "result" text field whenever "structured_output" is missing.
Wrap the command in a retry loop that re-runs the review until "structured_output" appears in the output.

questions.question: The pipeline delegates codebase scanning for each pull request to the Explore subagent. A teammate proposes that Explore also apply the minor formatting fixes it discovers while scanning. What should you tell them?

options.text: Instruct Explore in its prompt to use the "Edit" tool on each file where it finds a fix.
Have the main conversation apply the fixes after Explore reports, since Explore cannot edit files.
Invoke Explore at the "very thorough" level so the deeper pass also carries out the fixes it identifies.
Resume the completed Explore run and ask it to apply the fixes listed in its report.

questions.question: While tuning the automated review prompt interactively, you have corrected Claude on the same false-positive pattern three times in one session, but Claude keeps flagging it wrongly. What is the recommended next step?

options.text: Run /compact to summarize the conversation and continue correcting in the compressed context.
Have Claude rate its confidence in each flag and suppress the low-confidence findings.
Run /clear and restart with a more specific prompt that incorporates what you learned.
Repeat the correction with stronger emphasis such as IMPORTANT so the instruction takes priority.

questions.question: The pipeline runs a fresh non-interactive review on every push to an open pull request. When developers push follow-up commits, Claude reposts findings it already raised, and the duplicate comments are making developers trust the reviews less. What change prevents the duplicates?

options.text: Scope each re-review to the diff of only the newest commit so earlier files are never re-analyzed.
Have Claude assign a confidence score to each finding and suppress any below a fixed threshold.
Pass the prior review's findings into the prompt and instruct Claude to flag only new or unresolved issues.
Add a prompt instruction telling Claude never to repeat comments it has already posted on the pull request.

questions.question: The pipeline's nightly test-generation job keeps producing tests that duplicate cases already covered elsewhere in the suite and use assertion styles inconsistent with the team's existing tests. What change most effectively fixes both problems?
